AI.motivation: Calcium signals are noisy and temporally filtered, and paired neural-video data are limited, which makes reconstructing visual experience from calcium imaging hard.
AI.method: Layout and semantic controls derived from calcium activity condition a pretrained video diffusion model; the measured responses come from 7,863 V1 neurons in one mouse, and a stimulus-aligned virtual population of 116,705 neurons is assembled from encoding-model predictions across 11 independently recorded datasets.
AI.result: Held-out natural-movie clips are reconstructed with 81.4% all-pairs stimulus-identification accuracy, with the clearest gains over deterministic baselines in perceptual and semantic measures; perturbation and ablation analyses show that reconstruction depends on distributed, stimulus-specific population structure, with layout and semantic pathways providing complementary spatial and identity information; semantic dynamics are better preserved across clips.
AI.conclusion: Large-scale cortical population activity constrains the spatial, semantic and temporal structure of natural visual experience, providing a generative route to high-fidelity reconstruction of dynamic scenes.

title: MotionCore: A Latent Neural Simulator for Video Generation with Rigid-Body Dynamics
summary: Video generation models can produce highly realistic videos while generating physically inconsistent object motion. This limitation suggests that visual modeling alone may not provide a transferable representation of physical dynamics. We introduce MotionCore, a framework for learning physical dynamics via a learnable partial differential equation solver and focuses on rigid-body motion. We introduce a latent neural simulator learning to predict the evolution of object-level physical states from observed motion. Its predictions are then converted into spatially aligned latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model. The generator serves as a visual interface: it provides appearance and scene detail, while the learned dynamics model specifies the physical trajectory. To preserve this trajectory through the interface, MotionCore combines a diffusion-matching objective with a low-capacity decodability constraint on object identity and position. We evaluate MotionCore on public physical-consistency benchmarks and on paired data with known trajectories. Results indicate that MotionCore improves physical consistency and trajectory obedience in the evaluated rigid-body settings, while maintaining comparable visual quality. A controlled ablation protocol compares learned dynamics with an analytic prior and studies the choice of latent evolution processor.

AI.tldr: MotionCore learns a latent neural simulator for rigid-body dynamics and uses its predicted trajectories as spatially aligned latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model, improving physical consistency.
AI.motivation: Video generation models produce realistic video with physically inconsistent object motion, which suggests visual modeling alone does not provide a transferable representation of physical dynamics.
AI.method: A latent neural simulator predicts the evolution of object-level physical states from observed motion; its predictions become latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model, trained with a diffusion-matching objective plus a low-capacity decodability constraint on object identity and position.
AI.result: On public physical-consistency benchmarks and paired data with known trajectories, MotionCore improves physical consistency and trajectory obedience in the evaluated rigid-body settings while keeping visual quality comparable; a controlled ablation compares learned dynamics with an analytic prior and studies the choice of latent evolution processor.
AI.conclusion: Within the evaluated rigid-body settings, a learned dynamics model can specify the physical trajectory through a video generator that supplies appearance.

title: FANO: Anchored Forward-Noise Optimization for Diffusion Inverse Problems
comment: 26 pages, 9 figures, 8 tables. Preprint, under review
summary: Pre-trained diffusion models have become a widely adopted zero-shot prior for image inverse problems, among which annealed decoupling methods achieve leading reconstruction performance on nonlinear tasks. We find, however, that annealed methods that directly optimize the denoiser input $x_t$ exhibit radial drift in later layers: within-layer optimization drives the noise-component norm of $x_t$ away from its typical value, pushing the denoiser out of its high-performance regime and degrading reconstruction quality. To address this, we propose FANO (Anchored Forward-Noise Optimization). At each annealing layer, FANO fixes the previous denoiser estimate as an anchor and optimizes only the forward noise $e$, whose distribution is known, instead of $x_t$, thereby preserving the forward-diffusion structure of the denoiser input. The standard Gaussian prior on $e$ concentrates its norm near the typical value, and deviations degrade denoiser performance. We accordingly decompose $e$ in polar coordinates into a direction and a radial magnitude, and apply a soft potential to regulate the radius, keeping $x_t$ in the high-density region of the forward distribution. On multiple linear and nonlinear inverse problems, FANO matches the strongest current baselines on linear tasks and achieves consistent improvements on nonlinear tasks.

AI.tldr: FANO fixes radial drift in annealed diffusion inverse solvers by optimizing only the forward noise, anchored to the previous denoiser estimate, with its radius regulated in polar coordinates.
AI.motivation: Annealed methods that optimize the denoiser input x_t drift in noise-component norm in later layers, pushing the denoiser out of its high-performance regime and degrading reconstruction.
AI.method: At each annealing layer FANO fixes the previous denoiser estimate as an anchor and optimizes only the forward noise e, whose distribution is known; e is decomposed in polar coordinates into a direction and a radial magnitude, and a soft potential regulates the radius.
AI.result: On multiple linear and nonlinear inverse problems FANO matches the strongest current baselines on linear tasks and achieves consistent improvements on nonlinear tasks; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Keeping the denoiser input in the high-density region of the forward distribution improves reconstruction for nonlinear inverse problems.

title: UAV-Based Computer Vision for Cattle Detection and Feed Bunk Spatial Analysis
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 6 tables. Preprint of paper accepted in IEEE Transactions on AgriFood Electronics
summary: Beef cattle production is central to Brazilian agribusiness and faces growing demands for efficiency, sustainability, and animal welfare. Precision Livestock Farming (PLF) offers tools to address these challenges, particularly through monitoring feeding-related spatial patterns in confined systems. Feeding management plays a decisive role in animal performance, yet its evaluation still relies largely on subjective, labor-intensive visual inspections that are hard to scale and prone to bias. This work proposes a computer vision framework based on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) to quantify cattle alignment and spatial dispersion at the feed bunk under real-world feedlot conditions. A UAV dataset was collected during flight campaigns at a commercial feedlot in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. Images were manually annotated into cattle head and cattle back classes to support object detection and image-level spatial analysis of cattle distribution. You Only Look Once (YOLO) models, namely YOLOv8 and YOLOv11, were evaluated, with YOLOv8 small used for the downstream spatial analysis. The feed bunk region was segmented using the Segment Anything Model (SAM), and geometric metrics based on detected head positions were developed to characterize alignment, spacing regularity, and clustering. The selected detector achieved 84.30% mAP50 and 35.50% mAP50-95, with an inference time of approximately 2.7 ms per image on an NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti GPU. The resulting metrics distinguished representative regular and irregular spatial distributions by Root Mean Square Deviation - RMSD (1.06 m and 4.26 m), Coefficient of Variation - CV (42.70% and 96.31%), and clustering (0 and 2 clusters), respectively. These findings indicate that the proposed approach can provide indicators for assessing feed bunk spatial patterns in PLF.

AI.tldr: A UAV-based computer vision framework detects cattle heads and backs at a feedlot feed bunk and computes geometric metrics of alignment, spacing and clustering to quantify feeding spatial patterns.
AI.motivation: Evaluation of feeding management relies on subjective, labor-intensive visual inspection that is hard to scale and prone to bias, while precision livestock farming needs scalable indicators.
AI.method: UAV images from a commercial feedlot in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, are manually annotated into cattle head and cattle back classes; YOLOv8 and YOLOv11 are evaluated, with YOLOv8 small used for the downstream analysis; SAM segments the feed bunk, and metrics based on detected head positions characterize alignment, spacing regularity and clustering.
AI.result: The selected detector reaches 84.30% mAP50 and 35.50% mAP50-95 at about 2.7 ms per image on an NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti; RMSD is 1.06 m for a regular and 4.26 m for an irregular distribution, CV is 42.70% and 96.31%, and clusters number 0 and 2 respectively.
AI.conclusion: The approach can provide indicators for assessing feed bunk spatial patterns in precision livestock farming.

title: MESAM: Enhancing SAM2 for Few-Shot Segmentation through Semantic-Visual Memory Generation and Refinement
comment: 17pages, 12figures
summary: This paper investigates how to leverage the powerful capabilities of the Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) to tackle few-shot segmentation (FSS) tasks. One major challenge lies in the substantial appearance differences between the support and query images, which may diminish the effectiveness of the memory-matching process in SAM2. Through systematic analysis, we find that the memory generated based on the categorical semantic information is robust to this appearance divergence and is more compatible with SAM2. Based on these observations, we propose a new Memory-Enhanced SAM2 (MESAM) method, which first introduces a Semantic-Visual Memory Generation (SVMG) module to separately construct a query semantic memory, a query foreground visual memory, and a support adaptive visual memory. Then, in our designed Interactive Semantic Memory Refinement (ISMR) module, we further enrich the obtained semantic memory with fine-grained visual details, and suppress its misatcivated background responses. Extensive experiments on the PASCAL-$5^i$, COCO-$20^i$, and LVIS-$92^i$ datasets demonstrate that MESAM consistently outperforms existing FSS methods, achieving new state-of-the-art segmentation performance. Our source code is available at: \href{this https URL}{this https URL}.

AI.tldr: MESAM improves few-shot segmentation with SAM2 by building memory from categorical semantic information and refining it with fine-grained visual details, reaching new state-of-the-art results on PASCAL-5i, COCO-20i and LVIS-92i.
AI.motivation: Appearance differences between support and query images weaken SAM2's memory matching for few-shot segmentation.
AI.method: Semantic-Visual Memory Generation (SVMG) builds a query semantic memory, a query foreground visual memory and a support adaptive visual memory. Interactive Semantic Memory Refinement (ISMR) enriches the semantic memory with visual details and suppresses its misactivated background responses.
AI.result: MESAM consistently outperforms existing FSS methods on PASCAL-5i, COCO-20i and LVIS-92i, achieving new state-of-the-art segmentation performance.
AI.conclusion: Memory built from categorical semantics is robust to appearance divergence and more compatible with SAM2, so semantic memory is an effective basis for adapting SAM2 to few-shot segmentation.

title: MetricPose: Flexible 3D Human Pose Estimation with Depth and Geometric Cues
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, ICRA submission
summary: In this paper, we present a 3D human pose estimator that predicts metrically accurate human joint positions in the camera coordinate frame. This task requires recovering the configuration of the body joints, scale, and metric camera-local placement. In monocular images, body size and camera distance are coupled through perspective projection and therefore cannot be determined uniquely from image alone. This ambiguity can be reduced by combining three complementary sources of information: learned RGB priors, direct depth measurements, and geometric constraints (e.g., ground contact) from the environment. We extend a pretrained full-body estimator with optional metric depth and geometry-processing modules that improve camera-distance estimation and depth-guided body refinement while preserving RGB-only operation. The resulting unified model supports RGB, RGB-Ground, and RGB-D using shared learned parameters. Unlike pelvis-relative error, camera-local error also measures placement relative to the camera. Compared with the existing foundation model SAM 3D Body, our methods with RGB, RGB-Ground, and RGB-D modes reduce camera-local joint-position error by 12.16%, 31.00% and 54.61% respectively.

AI.tldr: MetricPose estimates 3D human joints in metric camera coordinates by extending a pretrained full-body estimator with optional metric depth and ground-geometry cues, in RGB, RGB-Ground and RGB-D modes.
AI.motivation: In monocular images body size and camera distance are coupled through perspective projection, so metric camera-local placement cannot be determined from RGB alone. Pelvis-relative error also does not measure placement relative to the camera.
AI.method: A pretrained full-body estimator is extended with optional metric depth and geometry-processing modules that improve camera-distance estimation and depth-guided body refinement. The three input modes share learned parameters, and RGB-only operation is preserved.
AI.result: Compared with SAM 3D Body, MetricPose reduces camera-local joint-position error by 12.16% (RGB), 31.00% (RGB-Ground) and 54.61% (RGB-D).
AI.conclusion: Adding depth and geometric constraints to RGB priors yields metrically accurate camera-local human pose in one unified model that still works from RGB alone.

title: Region-aware error triage for medical image segmentation with groupwise conformal risk control
comment: 22 pages, 7 figures, 12 tables. Submitted to Biomedical Signal Processing and Control (BSPC)
summary: Segmentation masks are increasingly reviewed rather than redrawn, which requires knowing where a mask is likely wrong. Learned error maps rank pixels by risk, but the number of pixels to warn is chosen ad hoc, and calibrating one warning threshold over all error pixels may leave errors far from the predicted contour under-flagged. We propose RACE-Triage, a post-hoc error triage framework that leaves the segmentation mask unchanged. A risk network is trained on out-of-fold predictions from backbone-independent inputs. The predicted contour partitions each image into a boundary band and a non-boundary region, and conformal risk control is applied separately in each region to bound the expected fraction of missed errors among cases with errors there. On ISIC 2018 dermoscopy and BUSI breast ultrasound (where patient identifiers are unavailable, so independence across images is assumed), pooled control met its overall target but missed on average 31.8% and 36.4% of non-boundary errors. Regional control reduced these fractions to 19.3% and 20.9% and raised the recall of size-filtered false-negative components from 0.722 to 0.818 and from 0.611 to 0.763. The mean warned area grew by 1.6 and 4.9 percentage points, and its 95th percentile reached 23.5% and 38.5%. The effect held across three seeds and a second backbone, and area-matched heuristics did not reproduce it. On the external PH$^2$ set, frozen thresholds exceeded both targets, whereas recalibration with 100 local images brought the mean over repeated splits below them. Regional calibration improves non-boundary error coverage at a measured increase in warned area.

AI.tldr: RACE-Triage is a post-hoc framework that flags likely segmentation errors without changing the mask, applying conformal risk control separately to a boundary band and the non-boundary region.
AI.motivation: The number of pixels to warn is chosen ad hoc, and a single warning threshold over all error pixels can leave errors far from the predicted contour under-flagged.
AI.method: A risk network is trained on out-of-fold predictions from backbone-independent inputs. The predicted contour splits each image into a boundary band and a non-boundary region, and conformal risk control is applied in each region to bound the expected fraction of missed errors among cases with errors there.
AI.result: On ISIC 2018 and BUSI, pooled control missed on average 31.8% and 36.4% of non-boundary errors. Regional control reduced these to 19.3% and 20.9%, raised the recall of size-filtered false-negative components from 0.722 to 0.818 and from 0.611 to 0.763, and grew the mean warned area by 1.6 and 4.9 percentage points. On the external PH2 set, frozen thresholds exceeded both targets, and recalibration with 100 local images brought the mean over repeated splits below them.
AI.conclusion: Regional calibration improves non-boundary error coverage at a measured increase in warned area. The independence of images across patients is assumed, not verified, because patient identifiers are unavailable.

title: Refer-CityFlow and M3Track: A Benchmark Dataset and Reference Framework for Language-Driven Multi-Target Multi-Camera Tracking
comment: Accepted for publication at the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027), Evaluations and Datasets Track. 10 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables
summary: Referring multi-object tracking enables users to specify targets through natural language, but existing Refer-MOT benchmarks primarily focus on single-camera settings. We formalize Referring Multi-Target Multi-Camera Tracking (Refer-MTMCT), where free-form queries specify identity-consistent trajectories to be recovered across a network of sequential, sparse-overlap cameras. We introduce Refer-CityFlow, a benchmark built on CityFlow's global cross-camera identity annotations and augmented with language queries requiring joint language grounding, cross-camera association, and spatio-temporal reasoning. Refer-CityFlow covers 96 videos from 40 roadside cameras with 660+ identity-consistent cross-camera trajectories, 4,362 trajectory-level descriptions, and 7,699 queries, including 1,699 real-user queries collected from 50 participants. Reference experiments on the four-camera Scenario 02 show that single-camera referring trackers reach 14.95-18.28 HOTA on real-user queries, while the evaluated cross-view method achieves about 0.05 HOTA in direct transfer. To establish reference performance, we provide M3Track, a modular multimodal reference framework in which a large language model (LLM)-based agent orchestrates interchangeable detection, tracking, and cross-camera association modules. M3Track reaches 44.10 HOTA and 65.40 IDF1 on the same real-user query set. The project repository is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper formalizes referring multi-target multi-camera tracking, introduces the Refer-CityFlow benchmark, and provides M3Track, an LLM-agent framework that reaches 44.10 HOTA and 65.40 IDF1 on real-user queries.
AI.motivation: Existing Refer-MOT benchmarks focus on single-camera settings and do not cover identity-consistent trajectories across sparse-overlap camera networks.
AI.method: Refer-CityFlow builds on CityFlow's global cross-camera identity annotations and adds language queries, including 1,699 real-user queries from 50 participants. M3Track is a modular framework in which an LLM-based agent orchestrates interchangeable detection, tracking and cross-camera association modules.
AI.result: On the four-camera Scenario 02, single-camera referring trackers reach 14.95 to 18.28 HOTA on real-user queries, while the evaluated cross-view method achieves about 0.05 HOTA in direct transfer. M3Track reaches 44.10 HOTA and 65.40 IDF1 on the same real-user query set.
AI.conclusion: Existing methods struggle badly with cross-camera referring tracking, and the modular agent framework provides a reference performance for the new benchmark.

title: Frontier3DBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for 3D Creation across Objects, Scenes, and Interactive Open Worlds
comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, 4 tables. Project page: this https URL
summary: Coding agents combine visual understanding with program execution, offering a new route to automated 3D creation. By translating images and instructions into editable programs, they bring reconstruction, generation, and editing into a shared workflow. Yet existing benchmarks fragment evaluation across task scopes and protocols, leaving their capabilities across construction levels unclear. We propose Frontier3DBench, a unified benchmark of 145 tasks across 9 categories spanning object, scene, and interactive open-world creation, with joint evaluation of appearance, structure, and behavior. Experiments with 11 model-harness configurations reveal strengths that vary by level: GPT-6.1-sol leads the object and scene levels and achieves the highest overall score of 66.02/100, whereas GPT-6-astra leads interactive world construction. However, all configurations score lower on reference reconstruction than on text-driven generation in object and scene tasks. Producing plausible content thus remains easier than reproducing specified geometry, layouts, and visual details. Moreover, generated worlds average 83.08/100 on local mechanisms but only 20.82 on motion clearance and 30.26 on stateful workflows: individual mechanisms often function, whereas complete activities that require coordinated actions and persistent state remain difficult. These results identify reference fidelity and coordinated activity completion as central bottlenecks for coding agents in 3D creation.

AI.tldr: Frontier3DBench is a 145-task benchmark for coding agents doing 3D creation across objects, scenes and interactive open worlds, in which the best configuration scores 66.02/100 overall.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks fragment evaluation across task scopes and protocols, so the capabilities of coding agents across construction levels remain unclear.
AI.method: Joint evaluation of appearance, structure and behavior over 9 categories spanning object, scene and interactive open-world creation, applied to 11 model-harness configurations.
AI.result: GPT-6.1-sol leads the object and scene levels with the highest overall score of 66.02/100, while GPT-6-astra leads interactive world construction. All configurations score lower on reference reconstruction than on text-driven generation. Generated worlds average 83.08/100 on local mechanisms but only 20.82 on motion clearance and 30.26 on stateful workflows.
AI.conclusion: Reference fidelity and coordinated, stateful activity completion are the central bottlenecks for coding agents in 3D creation.

title: Grounding-Aware Judge Reward Reinforcement Learning for Out-of-Domain Face Anti-Spoofing
summary: Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) must distinguish genuine faces from presentation attacks. A unified Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) is an attractive solution: it detects physical attacks (print, replay, mask) in one model and produces interpretable forensic evidence via Chain-of-Thought (CoT). A central obstacle to post-training such a model with reinforcement learning is that FAS reasoning has no rule-verifiable ground truth: only the binary verdict is checkable, while the reasoning chain cannot be verified by any hand-crafted rule. Optimizing the verdict alone is therefore a sparse, hackable signal. The model can reach the correct answer through a shortcut such as a false-rejection bias, which does not generalize. We address this with a grounding-aware judge reward. A 32B vision-language judge scores each reasoning chain against the image on evidence anchoring, logical coherence, and domain knowledge, turning the image itself into the verification signal. The reward is applied in a Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) stage after CoT supervised fine-tuning. It is the judge, rather than the RL objective, that supplies the process supervision a verdict-only reward cannot. Our study starts from a model that already performs well In-Domain (ID) after CoT-based supervised fine-tuning and asks how to improve its Out-of-Domain (OOD) generalization. We find that grounding-aware rewards are an effective means to that end. We validate the method on OOD generalization, where the reward reduces ACER on two physical benchmarks (LCC-FASD 0.288 to 0.273, MSU-MFSD 0.431 to 0.409) while preserving ID accuracy (CelebA-Spoof 0.033 to 0.035). Against ResNet-50/101 and CLIP-ViT-B/16 baselines, the MLLM dominates ID and matches or surpasses the strongest baseline OOD. To our knowledge this is the first use of LLM-as-judge process supervision for FAS.

AI.tldr: The paper post-trains a face anti-spoofing MLLM with GRPO using a grounding-aware reward from a 32B vision-language judge that scores reasoning chains against the image, improving out-of-domain generalization.
AI.motivation: FAS reasoning has no rule-verifiable ground truth, so a verdict-only reward is sparse and hackable: the model can reach correct answers through shortcuts such as a false-rejection bias that do not generalize.
AI.method: After CoT supervised fine-tuning, a Group Relative Policy Optimization stage uses a judge reward. A 32B vision-language judge scores each reasoning chain against the image on evidence anchoring, logical coherence and domain knowledge.
AI.result: The reward reduces ACER on LCC-FASD from 0.288 to 0.273 and on MSU-MFSD from 0.431 to 0.409, while CelebA-Spoof in-domain performance is preserved (0.033 to 0.035). Out of domain, the MLLM matches or surpasses the strongest ResNet-50/101 and CLIP-ViT-B/16 baselines.
AI.conclusion: Grounding-aware judge rewards supply the process supervision that a verdict-only reward lacks and improve out-of-domain generalization. The authors claim this is the first use of LLM-as-judge process supervision for FAS.

title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
summary: 3D part decomposition is a central capability for editable asset creation, yet existing workflows typically segment a completed mesh as a post-processing step, making the result sensitive to geometric artifacts, texture ambiguity, and limited part-level annotations. We present OmniLatent, a unified latent modeling framework for 3D part decomposition. Instead of predicting part labels in isolation, OmniLatent learns a shared latent space that jointly encodes geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs, allowing data-rich geometric and visual priors to support data-scarce part learning. Given a single input image, the base model generates geometry, deformation, texture, and surface part IDs in one pass, producing a part-aware 3D asset without a separate segmentation stage. We further tune the pretrained model for two extensions: a point-prompt adapter that maps arbitrary 3D point prompts with binary part IDs into latent tokens for full segmentation, refinement, and part subdivision, and an amodal part completion model that completes partial surface masks into a coherent full-object decomposition through dynamic per-part token allocation, cross-attention to the given geometry latent, and alternating part-local and global attention. Extensive experiments show that OmniLatent produces semantically meaningful part segmentations with precise boundaries, supports interactive part editing, and completes partial part observations while preserving global object consistency.

AI.tldr: OmniLatent is a unified latent model that generates geometry, deformation, texture and binary part IDs from a single image in one pass, producing part-aware 3D assets without a separate segmentation stage.
AI.motivation: Existing workflows segment a completed mesh as a post-processing step, which is sensitive to geometric artifacts, texture ambiguity and limited part-level annotations.
AI.method: A shared latent space jointly encodes geometry, deformation, appearance and binary part IDs, so data-rich priors support data-scarce part learning. A point-prompt adapter maps 3D point prompts with binary part IDs into latent tokens for segmentation, refinement and part subdivision. An amodal part completion model uses dynamic per-part token allocation, cross-attention to the geometry latent, and alternating part-local and global attention.
AI.result: Experiments show semantically meaningful part segmentations with precise boundaries, support for interactive part editing, and completion of partial part observations while preserving global object consistency. The abstract reports no numerical benchmark figures.
AI.conclusion: Jointly modeling part IDs with geometry and appearance in one latent space enables part-aware 3D generation and editing from a single image.

title: Emo-LiveSync: Real-Time Universal Lip Synchronization with Explicit Emotion Control
comment: Accepted to BMVC 2026, 23 pages, 16 figures
summary: Lip synchronization, the task of generating realistic lip movements synchronized with audio signals, is fundamental to applications such as film dubbing, virtual avatars, and digital content creation. Recent GAN-based methods offer computational efficiency but often lack visual fidelity, while diffusion-based approaches achieve high-quality results at the cost of substantial computational overhead. Moreover, most existing methods are limited to photo-realistic human faces, restricting their applicability to stylized characters and non-human entities. In this paper, we propose an efficient universal lip-sync video generation framework that achieves high-quality results without compromising computational efficiency. We build on LivePortrait, a warp-based portrait animation model, and introduce a training strategy that aligns audio signals to an implicit motion space by distilling knowledge from a pre-trained video-to-motion model. This enables real-time inference while maintaining high visual fidelity, and naturally generalizes to diverse stylistic characters beyond photo-realistic humans. Furthermore, we introduce an expressive control gate that enables explicit manipulation of emotional expressions for content enrichment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both visual quality and lip-sync accuracy while ensuring real-time inference.

AI.tldr: Emo-LiveSync is a real-time universal lip-sync framework built on LivePortrait, using distillation from a pretrained video-to-motion model and an expressive control gate for explicit emotion control.
AI.motivation: GAN-based methods are efficient but lack visual fidelity, diffusion-based methods are high quality but costly, and most existing methods are limited to photo-realistic human faces.
AI.method: Audio is aligned to the implicit motion space of the warp-based LivePortrait model by distilling knowledge from a pretrained video-to-motion model. An expressive control gate enables explicit manipulation of emotional expressions.
AI.result: The method achieves state-of-the-art visual quality and lip-sync accuracy while running in real time, and it generalizes to stylized characters and non-human entities.
AI.conclusion: Aligning audio to an implicit motion space gives real-time, high-fidelity lip-sync that generalizes beyond photo-realistic humans and supports emotion control.

title: Trajectory Forcing: Exploiting Diffusion Trajectories for Autoregressive Long Video Generation
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026
summary: Autoregressive (AR) modeling is arguably the only way to extend a fixed-length video diffusion model to longer or even streaming videos. However, existing AR diffusion methods use only the previously predicted chunk as context for the next, discarding the intermediate predictions that constitute the chunk's generation history. In contrast, conventional AR models such as LLMs condition on the entire history of preceding tokens. To this end, we propose Trajectory Forcing (TraF), an AR diffusion method that exploits the denoising trajectories of previous video chunks as context. TraF operates under two training regimes: (1) with ground-truth videos, where pseudo-trajectories are constructed from Gaussian interpolations and re-predicted by the model, and (2) with a teacher model, where real trajectories are obtained from the student's own denoising rollout. The first regime naturally provides a strong initialization for the second. On the 5-second VBench benchmark, TraF achieves a Total score of 85.15, outperforming Self Forcing (+0.84) and Causal Forcing (+1.11), with Quality and Semantic improving simultaneously. On 30-second generation---6$\times$ the training horizon---TraF achieves the highest overall quality among all compared methods.

AI.tldr: Trajectory Forcing conditions autoregressive video diffusion on the denoising trajectories of previous chunks rather than only their final output, improving long-video generation.
AI.motivation: Existing AR diffusion methods use only the previously predicted chunk as context and discard the intermediate predictions that form its generation history, whereas conventional AR models such as LLMs condition on the entire history.
AI.method: Two training regimes. With ground-truth videos, pseudo-trajectories are built from Gaussian interpolations and re-predicted by the model. With a teacher model, real trajectories come from the student's own denoising rollout. The first regime provides an initialization for the second.
AI.result: On the 5-second VBench benchmark, TraF scores a Total of 85.15, outperforming Self Forcing by 0.84 and Causal Forcing by 1.11, with Quality and Semantic both improving. On 30-second generation, 6 times the training horizon, it achieves the highest overall quality among compared methods.
AI.conclusion: Using previous denoising trajectories as context, not just clean chunks, improves autoregressive long video generation, including at 30 seconds, six times the training horizon.

title: BayesCrop: Real-Time Probabilistic Multi-Crop Video Reframing
comment: This paper is accepted by WACV 2027. We plan to publicly release the source code at this https URL
summary: Automatic video reframing is increasingly important for adapting landscape content to heterogeneous display formats. Existing methods typically predict a single deterministic crop, despite the subjective nature of reframing and the presence of multiple plausible regions of interest. We present \textbf{BayesCrop}, a real-time probabilistic framework for multi-crop video reframing. BayesCrop represents crop preferences using a two-component spatially isotropic Gaussian mixture over crop position and scale. Each component defines a representative reframing mode together with its local uncertainty, enabling both dual-view prediction and sampling of additional plausible crop candidates. For efficient video processing, we introduce an anchor-and-propagate strategy that performs neural prediction only on sparse anchor frames and propagates crop trajectories using motion vectors available from the compressed video bitstream. The resulting trajectories can be combined into a single output using a lightweight periodic view-switching strategy. Experiments on LIVE-YT-MC, LIVE-YT-VC++, and a multi-target long-video benchmark demonstrate competitive single-output localization, high multi-crop reference coverage, diverse yet coherent crop hypotheses, and stable perceptual quality. BayesCrop achieves real-time throughput of 112 FPS at the default operating point, while sampling from the learned distributions further improves reference coverage beyond the two representative crop means.

AI.tldr: BayesCrop is a real-time probabilistic framework for video reframing that models crop preferences with a two-component Gaussian mixture, giving dual-view outputs and sampled crop candidates at 112 FPS.
AI.motivation: Existing methods predict a single deterministic crop, although reframing is subjective and several regions of interest may be plausible.
AI.method: Crop position and scale are modeled by a two-component spatially isotropic Gaussian mixture. An anchor-and-propagate strategy runs neural prediction on sparse anchor frames and propagates crop trajectories with motion vectors from the compressed bitstream. A lightweight periodic view-switching strategy combines the trajectories into one output.
AI.result: On LIVE-YT-MC, LIVE-YT-VC++ and a multi-target long-video benchmark, BayesCrop shows competitive single-output localization, high multi-crop reference coverage, diverse yet coherent crop hypotheses and stable perceptual quality. It runs at 112 FPS at the default operating point, and sampling from the learned distributions further improves reference coverage beyond the two mode means.
AI.conclusion: Modeling reframing as a distribution yields multiple plausible crops at real-time speed, and sampling from the learned distribution adds coverage beyond the two representative crops.

title: Finite-sample Calibration Guarantees for Binary Segmentation
comment: Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research 10/2026
summary: Machine learning based segmentation models are frequently miscalibrated, producing for each pixel a label prediction whose associated confidence does not accurately reflect the true underlying probability. This limitation is particularly critical in high-stakes applications such as medical image segmentation. Although several calibration methods have been proposed, only a small subset of them provides theoretical guarantees on the calibration error, i.e., they do not typically ensure that, with high probability, the model exhibits a low calibration error. In this work, we develop a post-hoc calibration method for which formal calibration guarantees can be established. To achieve this, we derive from standard concentration inequalities an improved theoretical bound that explicitly accounts for the spatial dependence inherent in binary segmentation outputs. We empirically demonstrate that the proposed calibrator satisfies the derived guarantee and outperforms existing post-hoc calibration approaches.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a post-hoc calibrator for binary segmentation with formal finite-sample calibration guarantees, derived from concentration inequalities that account for spatial dependence between pixels.
AI.motivation: Segmentation models are often miscalibrated, and most calibration methods do not guarantee that calibration error is low with high probability, which matters in high-stakes uses such as medical image segmentation.
AI.method: An improved theoretical bound, derived from standard concentration inequalities, explicitly accounts for the spatial dependence in binary segmentation outputs. A post-hoc calibration method is built so that this guarantee can be established.
AI.result: The authors show empirically that the calibrator satisfies the derived guarantee and outperforms existing post-hoc calibration approaches. The abstract gives no numerical results.
AI.conclusion: Accounting for spatial dependence in the concentration bound makes provable calibration guarantees possible for binary segmentation.

title: CoMET: Tracking the Shared Pose Error of Roadside Messages for Asynchronous Vehicle-Infrastructure Cooperative 3D Detection
comment: 25 pages, 4 figures. Code and experimental results archived at this https URL
summary: A roadside sensor can detect vehicles hidden from the ego vehicle, but a pose error shifts every detection in the same message. We study asynchronous vehicle-infrastructure cooperative 3D detection on V2X-Seq using only information available at decision time, without ground truth, future frames, or per-pair calibration offsets at inference. Objects seen by both sensors reveal the shared translation, but even at zero added delay, 38% of validation messages have no matched pair. We propose CoMET (Common-Mode Error Tracking), which estimates this translation over time. At each message arrival, CoMET matches vehicle and roadside detections, estimates the offset from mutually nearest pairs, and updates a Kalman filter for that sender. When no pair matches, the filter carries its estimate forward. The correction applies to all roadside boxes, including those unseen by the ego vehicle. The estimator has no learned parameters; a separate frozen head ranks the merged detections. Across four delays from 0 to 400 ms on 21 validation sequences, CoMET averages 66.63 bird's-eye-view AP at IoU 0.7, compared with 63.18 for the same late fusion using uncorrected online poses and 62.96 for the best intermediate-fusion baseline. Across five detectors from three architectures, CoMET gains 2.2 to 3.5 AP points over online poses and 0.3 to 0.6 over estimating the offset from the current message alone. We find that the benchmark uses a zero offset as a placeholder in 28% of validation messages and that its offset search reaches the boundary in 45% of the rest. These offsets affect the labels for objects seen only from the roadside. Under two alternative label references, CoMET improves on uncorrected online poses in every evaluated population. Retraining intermediate fusion with CoMET poses and corrected labels improves detection on all three architectures tested, with statistically significant gains on two.

AI.tldr: CoMET tracks the shared translation error of roadside poses over time with a per-sender Kalman filter and applies the correction to all roadside boxes, with no learned parameters in the estimator, for asynchronous vehicle-infrastructure cooperative 3D detection.
AI.motivation: A roadside pose error shifts every detection in the same message. Even at zero added delay, 38% of validation messages have no matched vehicle-roadside pair, so the offset cannot always be estimated from the current message alone.
AI.method: At each message arrival, CoMET matches vehicle and roadside detections, estimates the offset from mutually nearest pairs, and updates a Kalman filter for that sender. When no pair matches, the filter carries its estimate forward. The correction applies to all roadside boxes, including those unseen by the ego vehicle.
AI.result: Across four delays from 0 to 400 ms on 21 validation sequences, CoMET averages 66.63 BEV AP at IoU 0.7, compared with 63.18 for late fusion with uncorrected online poses and 62.96 for the best intermediate-fusion baseline. Across five detectors from three architectures, it gains 2.2 to 3.5 AP over online poses and 0.3 to 0.6 over estimating the offset from the current message alone.
AI.conclusion: The benchmark's offset labels are unreliable, with a zero placeholder in 28% of validation messages and the offset search reaching its boundary in 45% of the rest. CoMET improves on uncorrected online poses under two alternative label references, and retraining intermediate fusion with CoMET poses and corrected labels improves detection on all three architectures tested.

title: Look Closer, Align Better: Explicit Visual Attributes for Robust EEG-to-Image Decoding
summary: EEG-to-image retrieval commonly aligns neural responses with representations from pretrained vision encoders. However, these representations may underrepresent fine-grained visual details needed to distinguish semantically similar images. To address this limitation, we first investigate the EEG decodability and complementary predictive value of explicit visual attributes, identifying visual cues that capture EEG-relevant information beyond pretrained representations. Building on these findings, we propose AttrEcho, a framework that enriches pretrained visual representations with complementary, spatially aligned visual attributes. Specifically, Region-Aligned Visual Attribute Fusion (RAVF) integrates EEG-relevant local visual attributes with spatially corresponding pretrained features through a learnable signed residual gate. We further employ Feature Token Aggregation (FTA), which learns dimension-specific weights across regions to aggregate refined visual features for contrastive alignment with EEG representations. Experiments on THINGS-EEG demonstrate that AttrEcho achieves 94.8% Top-1 and 99.7% Top-5 accuracy in intra-subject 200-way retrieval, while maintaining 82.1% Top-1 accuracy as the gallery expands to 1,600 images with same-concept distractors. AttrEcho also achieves 25.3% Top-1 and 53.0% Top-5 accuracy in inter-subject retrieval. These results highlight the importance of EEG-relevant visual attributes and spatially aligned fusion for fine-grained EEG-to-image retrieval.

AI.tldr: AttrEcho enriches pretrained visual features with spatially aligned explicit visual attributes for EEG-to-image retrieval, reaching 94.8% Top-1 accuracy in intra-subject 200-way retrieval on THINGS-EEG.
AI.motivation: Pretrained vision encoder representations may underrepresent the fine-grained visual details needed to distinguish semantically similar images in EEG-to-image retrieval.
AI.method: Region-Aligned Visual Attribute Fusion (RAVF) combines EEG-relevant local visual attributes with spatially corresponding pretrained features through a learnable signed residual gate. Feature Token Aggregation (FTA) learns dimension-specific weights across regions to aggregate refined visual features for contrastive alignment with EEG representations.
AI.result: On THINGS-EEG, intra-subject 200-way retrieval reaches 94.8% Top-1 and 99.7% Top-5. With the gallery expanded to 1,600 images with same-concept distractors, Top-1 accuracy remains 82.1%. Inter-subject retrieval reaches 25.3% Top-1 and 53.0% Top-5.
AI.conclusion: EEG-relevant visual attributes and spatially aligned fusion matter for fine-grained EEG-to-image retrieval.

title: TouchAnnotator: Multi-Source Tactile Supervision with Privileged-View Distillation
summary: Egocentric video captures human-object interaction at scale but rarely includes tactile labels for hidden contact and pressure. We introduce TouchAnnotator, an ego-only bimanual tactile annotator trained with multi-source tactile supervision and privileged-view distillation. A canonical hand field unifies glove pressure, geometry-derived human contact, and robot fingertip deformation from six datasets and three embodiments, while source-aware masks preserve valid targets. During training, an EMA teacher observes synchronized ego and wrist views and distills hand-local representations and tactile predictions into a student that uses only ego video and estimated pose at inference. Compact past-clip memory supplies temporal context. We evaluate on EgoTouch, zero-shot FPHA transfer, and 860 synchronized glove recordings. The model transfers to bare-hand contact and produces qualitatively coherent tactile responses across bare-hand, gloved-hand, and robot embodiments. On measured recordings, it improves temporal accuracy by 5.38 points and Volumetric IoU by 5.02 points under a shared protocol. These results show that heterogeneous human--robot supervision and privileged training views can turn egocentric video into dense tactile annotations.

AI.tldr: TouchAnnotator is an ego-only bimanual tactile annotator that predicts dense tactile labels from egocentric video, trained with multi-source tactile supervision and privileged-view distillation from an EMA teacher that also sees wrist views.
AI.motivation: Egocentric video of human-object interaction rarely includes tactile labels for hidden contact and pressure.
AI.method: A canonical hand field unifies glove pressure, geometry-derived human contact and robot fingertip deformation from six datasets and three embodiments, with source-aware masks. An EMA teacher observing synchronized ego and wrist views distills hand-local representations and tactile predictions into a student that uses only ego video and estimated pose. A compact past-clip memory supplies temporal context.
AI.result: Evaluated on EgoTouch, zero-shot FPHA transfer and 860 synchronized glove recordings, the model improves temporal accuracy by 5.38 points and Volumetric IoU by 5.02 points on measured recordings under a shared protocol. It transfers to bare-hand contact and produces qualitatively coherent tactile responses across bare-hand, gloved-hand and robot embodiments.
AI.conclusion: Heterogeneous human-robot supervision and privileged training views can turn egocentric video into dense tactile annotations.

title: DINO-Nucleus: Multi-Level Self-Supervised Features for Nucleus Instance Segmentation
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures
summary: Nucleus instance segmentation and counting are essential for quantitative microscopy, enabling reliable analysis of cell populations, tissue organization, and disease-related changes. However, accurately separating touching nuclei remains difficult, and many existing approaches rely on complex models or sensitive post-processing procedures. We present DINO-Nucleus, a parameter-efficient framework that leverages multi-level self-supervised DINOv2 representations for nucleus instance segmentation and counting. The model jointly predicts nucleus regions, pixel-wise instance flows, and explicit nucleus centers, while a consistency objective encourages the predicted flows to converge toward their corresponding centers. Multi-level transformer features provide complementary spatial and semantic information, and the pretrained backbone is adapted using lightweight LoRA modules to reduce fine-tuning cost. Experimental results show that DINO-Nucleus achieves strong segmentation and counting performance with parameter-efficient backbone adaptation. These findings demonstrate that parameter-efficient adaptation of multi-level self-supervised features can provide an effective solution for nucleus instance segmentation in microscopy images.

AI.tldr: DINO-Nucleus adapts multi-level DINOv2 features with LoRA modules to jointly predict nucleus regions, pixel-wise instance flows and explicit nucleus centers for instance segmentation and counting in microscopy.
AI.motivation: Accurately separating touching nuclei remains difficult, and many existing approaches rely on complex models or sensitive post-processing.
AI.method: Multi-level transformer features from DINOv2 supply complementary spatial and semantic information, and the pretrained backbone is adapted with lightweight LoRA modules. A consistency objective encourages the predicted flows to converge toward their corresponding centers.
AI.result: The abstract reports strong segmentation and counting performance with parameter-efficient backbone adaptation. It gives no quantitative figures, datasets or baselines.
AI.conclusion: Parameter-efficient adaptation of multi-level self-supervised features is presented as an effective solution for nucleus instance segmentation in microscopy.

title: Bootstrap Your Own AV-Proxies: Adaptive Contrastive and Prototype Learning for Audio-Visual Segmentation
comment: Accepted to CVPR 2026
summary: Audio-Visual Segmentation (AVS) aims to accurately segment sounding objects in video frames by leveraging audio-visual correspondence cues. However, it remains challenging due to the intrinsic semantic incompleteness within a single modality and the semantic gap between audio and visual representations. Traditional feature-fusion decoding approaches struggle to suppress fusion noise effectively, while recent methods that incorporate data-dependent priors often increase the complexity of modeling audio-visual correlations, leading to poor cross-domain generalization. To address these issues, we propose a novel adaptive contrastive and prototype learning framework, BYOAVP, for AVS. Specifically, we design a Self-Supervised Audio Enhancement (SSAE) module that introduces contrastive learning to adaptively align audio representations with gradient-blocked visual embeddings, thus narrowing the semantic gap between modalities. Furthermore, a Dynamic Prototype Constraint (DPC) module is developed to refine pixel-wise category perception via momentum-based prototype updating, while enhancing localization of sounding regions through cross-modal interaction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves SOTA performance across two AVS benchmarks and six sub-tasks, exhibiting strong robustness and generalization ability.

AI.tldr: BYOAVP is an audio-visual segmentation framework that aligns audio with gradient-blocked visual embeddings through contrastive learning and refines pixel categories with momentum-updated dynamic prototypes, reporting SOTA performance on two benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Semantic incompleteness within each modality and the semantic gap between audio and visual representations make feature fusion noisy, while data-dependent priors add modeling complexity and hurt cross-domain generalization.
AI.method: Self-Supervised Audio Enhancement (SSAE) uses contrastive learning to adaptively align audio representations with gradient-blocked visual embeddings. Dynamic Prototype Constraint (DPC) refines pixel-wise category perception through momentum-based prototype updating and enhances localization of sounding regions via cross-modal interaction.
AI.result: The method achieves SOTA performance across two AVS benchmarks and six sub-tasks, with strong robustness and generalization claimed. The abstract gives no numerical values.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive contrastive alignment and prototype learning give robust, generalizable audio-visual segmentation.

title: InstantHMR : Real-Time Human Mesh Recovery on Your Phone
summary: Real-time 3D human mesh recovery from a single image on mobile devices is a challenging problem with many applications, including robotics, biomechanics, AR/VR, and exergames. Current state-of-the-art models are either too slow to run efficiently on mobile devices or sacrifice accuracy for speed. We present InstantHMR, a family of open-source single-image regressors suited for mobile inference, based on the Momentum Human Rig (MHR) parametric model and trained exclusively on publicly available annotations from the SAM 3D Body dataset. Our approach achieves remarkable performance on a Samsung Galaxy S23 NPU, recovering a 6,890-vertex body mesh in 5.5 ms per person, and 0.98 ms on an NVIDIA RTX 4070 GPU. This speed surpasses all existing methods we evaluated. On mobile, it is 12x faster than the single mobile-compatible method that slightly outperforms ours in accuracy, while achieving competitive accuracy with 40.0 mm PA-MPJPE on 3DPW, 48.8 mm on EMDB and 41.7 mm on RICH. To ensure fair comparisons, we re-evaluate 11 state-of-the-art methods under a unified protocol aligned with the closest MHR-based competitors, including Meta's official MHR-to-SMPL conversion, and report their reproduction results. Additionally, we measure latency across eight different targets, ranging from desktop TensorRT to two phone NPUs. Code and models are available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: InstantHMR is a family of open-source single-image human mesh regressors built on the MHR parametric model for real-time mobile inference, recovering a body mesh in 5.5 ms per person on a Samsung Galaxy S23 NPU.
AI.motivation: Current state-of-the-art human mesh recovery models are either too slow to run efficiently on mobile devices or sacrifice accuracy for speed.
AI.method: The regressors are based on the Momentum Human Rig (MHR) parametric model and trained only on publicly available annotations from the SAM 3D Body dataset. Latency is measured across eight targets, from desktop TensorRT to two phone NPUs.
AI.result: The model recovers a 6,890-vertex body mesh in 5.5 ms per person on the Galaxy S23 NPU and 0.98 ms on an NVIDIA RTX 4070 GPU. On mobile it is 12x faster than the single mobile-compatible method that slightly outperforms it in accuracy. PA-MPJPE is 40.0 mm on 3DPW, 48.8 mm on EMDB and 41.7 mm on RICH. Eleven state-of-the-art methods are re-evaluated under a unified protocol.
AI.conclusion: InstantHMR runs faster than all existing methods evaluated while staying competitive in accuracy, and the code and models are released.

title: T2I Models Rarely Invert Negation but Often Fail to Suppress Negated Concepts: Benchmarking Negation Suppression in Text-to-Image Generation
comment: Accepted at WACV 2027. Code and data: this https URL
summary: Text-to-image diffusion models often fail to suppress explicitly negated concepts, such as a lamp for "a desk without a lamp." We introduce T2I-NSI, a benchmark and metric for measuring negation sensitivity in text-to-image generation. It pairs each negated prompt with a canonical positive counterpart and factorizes negation by linguistic form (lexical/semantic, morphological, syntactic) and target type (objects, attributes, relations, compositions, and nested cases). The benchmark contains 759,869 paired prompt atoms over a 5,082-object catalog, with 916,272 images (911,982 open-weights, 4,290 closed-source), scored by a Basic CLIP estimator and a Robust ensemble of CLIP, VQA and open-vocabulary detection. Negation sensitivity is low: open-weights generators score NSI <= 0.038, while GPT-Image-1.5 and Gemini-2.5-Flash-Image reach about 0.09. The dominant failure is under-suppression rather than misdirection. Inverse interpretation is essentially absent (0.00% across over 450K atom-model evaluations), whereas models render the concept under both prompts on 8-19% of atoms and only partly suppress it on a further 9-25%; most remaining atoms are too weakly rendered to label. A blinded human study (420 atoms, nine annotators) corroborates the near-absence of inversion and the high persistence rate, and a matched-prompt comparison shows the open-versus-closed gap (~3.5x) is not a prompt-generator artifact. Code and data: this https URL

AI.tldr: T2I-NSI is a benchmark and metric for negation sensitivity in text-to-image generation, showing that models rarely invert negation and often fail to suppress negated concepts.
AI.motivation: Text-to-image diffusion models often fail to suppress explicitly negated concepts, such as a lamp in "a desk without a lamp".
AI.method: Each negated prompt is paired with a canonical positive counterpart, and negation is factorized by linguistic form (lexical/semantic, morphological, syntactic) and target type (objects, attributes, relations, compositions, nested cases). The benchmark has 759,869 paired prompt atoms over a 5,082-object catalog and 916,272 images, scored by a Basic CLIP estimator and a Robust ensemble of CLIP, VQA and open-vocabulary detection, with a blinded human study of 420 atoms.
AI.result: Open-weights generators score NSI at most 0.038, while GPT-Image-1.5 and Gemini-2.5-Flash-Image reach about 0.09. Inverse interpretation is essentially absent (0.00% across over 450K atom-model evaluations). Models render the concept under both prompts on 8-19% of atoms and partly suppress it on a further 9-25%. The open-versus-closed gap is about 3.5x and is not a prompt-generator artifact.
AI.conclusion: The dominant failure is under-suppression rather than misdirection, so the remaining gap lies in suppressing negated content rather than inverting its meaning.

title: Interpretable Context-Aware Multi-Label Retinal Classification with Dual-Hub Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network
summary: Multi-label retinal screening requires capturing co-occurring pathologies and clinical context, yet standard multimodal fusion remains opaque. We propose a dual-hub heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) that couples spatial fundus features and structured clinical covariates through cross-modal message passing while providing inherent interpretability. Rather than relying on post-hoc saliency approximations, our architecture exposes multi-level decision pathways during forward aggregation: spatially biased self-attention captures lesion-level patch interactions, while modality-specific graph attention coefficients explicitly quantify the contribution of visual regions and clinical risk factors to each disease node. Evaluated on the BRSET dataset (16,266 photographs from 8,524 patients), the proposed model achieves 76.1% Macro-AUPRC across seven conditions, matching or exceeding image-only (75.9%) and ResNet-50+MLP fusion (75.9%) baselines, with largest contextual gains in macular edema (+3.5%) and diabetic retinopathy (+2.1%). Codebase is available at: this https URL.

AI.tldr: A dual-hub heterogeneous graph neural network fuses fundus image patches with clinical covariates for multi-label retinal classification, with interpretability built into the forward pass rather than from post-hoc saliency.
AI.motivation: Standard multimodal fusion for multi-label retinal screening is opaque, yet co-occurring pathologies and clinical context need to be captured.
AI.method: Cross-modal message passing couples spatial fundus features with structured clinical covariates. Spatially biased self-attention captures lesion-level patch interactions, and modality-specific graph attention coefficients quantify the contribution of visual regions and clinical risk factors to each disease node.
AI.result: On BRSET (16,266 photographs from 8,524 patients), the model reaches 76.1% Macro-AUPRC across seven conditions, versus 75.9% for image-only and ResNet-50+MLP fusion baselines, with the largest contextual gains in macular edema (+3.5%) and diabetic retinopathy (+2.1%).
AI.conclusion: Clinical context gives a small overall gain over image-only baselines, with interpretable decision pathways built into the architecture.

title: Keyline Detection with YOLO: Runway Perception for Vision-Based Aircraft Landing
comment: WACV 2027
summary: Modern object detectors can predict keypoints as per-object geometric features, but keypoints are inherently vulnerable to occlusion and truncation. Object edges can provide complementary information, often remaining observable even when partially occluded or when their defining endpoints leave the field of view. We therefore introduce object keyline detection, the task of predicting a fixed, semantically ordered set of infinite lines per object instance. Unlike the outputs of general line-segment detectors, each keyline is associated with an object instance and identified by a semantic index, providing a line-level analog of keypoints. To solve this task, we extend YOLO with keyline prediction parameterized in continuous Hesse-normal form $[\rho,\cos\theta,\sin\theta]$, and introduce Object Keyline Similarity (OKLS), which serves as an evaluation metric, target assignment signal, and regression loss. We instantiate this formulation on runway perception in vision-based landing, a motivating example containing semantic linear features that remain partially observable throughout the approach. Experiments show that our representation achieves the highest detection accuracy among four evaluated line parameterizations, and keylines integrate directly into standard YOLO heads as additional output channels without degrading keypoint performance or adding meaningful latency.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces object keyline detection, predicting a fixed, semantically ordered set of infinite lines per object by extending YOLO with keyline prediction in Hesse normal form and an OKLS metric, instantiated for runway perception in vision-based landing.
AI.motivation: Keypoints are vulnerable to occlusion and truncation, while object edges often remain observable, and general line-segment detectors do not associate lines with object instances or semantic indices.
AI.method: Keylines are parameterized in continuous Hesse normal form [rho, cos theta, sin theta]. Object Keyline Similarity (OKLS) serves as the evaluation metric, target assignment signal and regression loss. Keylines are integrated into standard YOLO heads as additional output channels.
AI.result: The representation achieves the highest detection accuracy among four evaluated line parameterizations. Keylines integrate without degrading keypoint performance or adding meaningful latency.
AI.conclusion: Keylines provide a line-level analog of keypoints that can be added to standard detectors at little cost, shown here on runway perception.

title: RegNC-Mamba3: Shared Structural Feature Learning Using Non-Causal State Space Principles for Multi-Modal Image Registration
summary: The main challenge of multi-modal image registration is shared structural feature extraction with higher accuracy and lower computational complexity. Compared with a State Space Model (SSM), the State Space Principles (SSP) formulation of Mamba-3 uses a more accurate discretization with lower truncation error while maintaining linear complexity. However, vanilla SSP is designed for natural language processing (NLP) and is not directly suitable for images. To address this issue, we propose a novel non-causal SSP (NC-SSP) with shared structure awareness and develop a coarse-to-fine registration method named RegNC-Mamba3. First, NC-SSP is designed to eliminate the dependence of the integral computation on the scanning path. By combining relative-weight normalization with aggregation over all circular scan paths, NC-SSP constructs a globally hidden state without long-range decay, which provides a wider receptive field and higher efficiency than the original Mamba-3. Second, NC-SSP is modified to strengthen the extraction of cross-modal structural features. When computing hidden states and feature interactions, we construct complex-valued sequences in NC-SSP by applying learnable Log-Gabor kernels, with different orientations to each head for frequency-domain modulation. This improves the perception of shared structural information across modalities and increases both registration accuracy and quality. Experiments on VIS-SAR and VIS-IR demonstrate that RegNC-Mamba3 outperforms the compared detector-based and semi-dense multi-modal registration methods.

AI.tldr: RegNC-Mamba3 is a coarse-to-fine multi-modal image registration method built on a non-causal state space principle (NC-SSP) that removes dependence on the scanning path and adds Log-Gabor-modulated complex-valued features for shared structure. It outperforms the compared detector-based and semi-dense registration methods on VIS-SAR and VIS-IR.
AI.motivation: Multi-modal registration needs accurate shared structural feature extraction at low computational cost, but the vanilla state space principles (SSP) of Mamba-3 are designed for NLP and are not directly suitable for images.
AI.method: NC-SSP removes dependence of the integral computation on the scanning path by combining relative-weight normalization with aggregation over all circular scan paths, which gives a globally hidden state without long-range decay; learnable Log-Gabor kernels with per-head orientations build complex-valued sequences that modulate features in the frequency domain to strengthen cross-modal structure.
AI.result: RegNC-Mamba3 outperforms the compared detector-based and semi-dense multi-modal registration methods on the VIS-SAR and VIS-IR experiments, improving registration accuracy and quality.
AI.conclusion: NC-SSP extends state space modelling to image registration with a wider receptive field and higher efficiency than the original Mamba-3, and it improves perception of structure shared across modalities.

title: A Bridge from Paste to Place: Physics-Guided One-Step Image Composition via Object-Scene Interaction
summary: Realistic image composition must make a pasted object appear naturally present in a scene while preserving the fine details of both foreground and background. Reference-based insertion methods can change object pose and appearance, while foreground harmonization methods and shadow-specific synthesis methods each address only part of this task. An efficient, unified solution to this task remains an open challenge. We introduce Paste2Place, an end-to-end, physics-guided flow-based model that learns a direct, one-step latent bridge from pasted inputs to realistic composites, guided by explicit albedo-shading-residual decomposition and recomposition within the model. To support model training and evaluation, we develop a Blender rendering and validation pipeline to generate paired composites with physical annotations, and construct real-scene pairs from open-source object-removal data. This effort yields 86,273 training pairs and a 1,500-example benchmark. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that Paste2Place achieves substantial advantages in image composition quality and inference speed. Overall, our work provides a clear task definition and an effective solution for image composition, and fills a gap in large-scale, high-quality datasets and benchmarks for training and evaluating image composition.

AI.tldr: Paste2Place is an end-to-end, physics-guided flow-based model that learns a one-step latent bridge from pasted object inputs to realistic composites, and it comes with a training set of 86,273 pairs and a 1,500-example benchmark.
AI.motivation: Reference-based insertion, foreground harmonization and shadow-specific synthesis each address only part of image composition, and an efficient unified solution together with large-scale, high-quality datasets and benchmarks has been lacking.
AI.method: The model uses explicit albedo-shading-residual decomposition and recomposition inside a flow-based network; training pairs come from a Blender rendering and validation pipeline with physical annotations, plus real-scene pairs built from open-source object-removal data.
AI.result: In extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments Paste2Place achieves substantial advantages in image composition quality and inference speed, trained on 86,273 pairs and evaluated on a 1,500-example benchmark.
AI.conclusion: The work gives image composition a clear task definition and an effective unified solution, and it fills a gap in large-scale datasets and benchmarks for training and evaluating composition.

title: The Role Of Recurrent Refinement In Medical Image Segmentation
summary: While feed-forward segmentation networks perform well on large cohorts, they degrade in constrained clinical settings with few training samples and imaging artifacts. Human vision, by contrast, remains robust under these conditions, a property partly attributed to the recurrent and feedback connectivity of the visual cortex, which refines visual information over time. Inspired by this, we append lightweight recurrent refinement blocks to segmentation backbones, namely Conditional Random Fields (CRFs), modern Hopfield networks and convolutional GRUs, and study their behaviour as the number of iterations increases at test time (including beyond the training horizon). Evaluated on two open-source datasets, Kvasir- SEG and ARCADE, our recurrent blocks add less than 1.5% parameters and yield gains on clean data (up to 1.4 pp) and under noise (up to 17 pp) while reducing HD95. Code is available at this https URL .

AI.tldr: Lightweight recurrent refinement blocks (conditional random fields, modern Hopfield networks and convolutional GRUs) appended to segmentation backbones improve medical image segmentation while adding less than 1.5% parameters, with the largest gains under noise.
AI.motivation: Feed-forward segmentation networks degrade in constrained clinical settings with few training samples and imaging artifacts, whereas human vision stays robust, partly because of the recurrent and feedback connectivity of the visual cortex.
AI.method: Recurrent refinement blocks are appended to segmentation backbones, namely CRFs, modern Hopfield networks and convolutional GRUs, and their behaviour is studied as the number of test-time iterations increases, including beyond the training horizon.
AI.result: On Kvasir-SEG and ARCADE the recurrent blocks add less than 1.5% parameters, yield gains on clean data of up to 1.4 pp and under noise of up to 17 pp, and reduce HD95.
AI.conclusion: Recurrent refinement is a low-cost way to make segmentation more robust to noise and limited data, and the iteration behaviour is studied as a route to more robust segmentation.

title: Overview of the ImageCLEFmedical 2026 GANs task: Exploring fingerprint detection, privacy leakage, and synthetic medical image generation
comment: CLEF 2026 Working Notes, 21-24 September 2026, Jena, Germany
summary: The 2026 ImageCLEFmedical GANs Task Exploring Fingerprint Detection, Privacy Leakage, and Synthetic Medical Image Generation continues to investigate privacy and security concerns around using patient data to generate synthetic medical images, now in its fourth edition. This edition introduces three complementary subtasks: the first extends prior editions by asking participants to detect which real images were used in training a Generative Adversarial Network to produce given synthetic outputs; the second is a novel subtask requiring participants to identify which latent vector produced each synthetic image, probing the faithfulness and reversibility of the latent-to-image mapping; the third asks participants to generate privacy-preserving CT slices, quantifying the trade-off between image fidelity and patient privacy. Ground-truth annotations and benchmark datasets of real and GAN-generated lung CT slices are provided for all subtasks. Evaluation is based on Cohen's Kappa for Subtask 1, matching accuracy for Subtask 2, and a combination of FID and Privacy Preservation Score (PPS) for Subtask 3. Overall, 37 teams registered for the task, with 10 teams submitting runs across subtasks and 6 teams submitting working notes papers. This paper presents an overview of the task setup, datasets, evaluation metrics, and summarises the approaches and results of participating teams.

AI.tldr: This is the overview of the 2026 ImageCLEFmedical GANs task, which has three subtasks on detecting training images, identifying latent vectors, and generating privacy-preserving lung CT slices; 37 teams registered and 10 submitted runs.
AI.motivation: Using patient data to train GANs for synthetic medical images raises privacy and security concerns, which this fourth edition of the task series continues to investigate.
AI.method: Subtask 1 asks participants to detect which real images were used to train a GAN that produced given synthetic outputs, subtask 2 asks which latent vector produced each synthetic image, and subtask 3 asks for privacy-preserving CT slices; ground-truth annotations and benchmark datasets of real and GAN-generated lung CT slices are provided.
AI.result: Evaluation uses Cohen's Kappa for subtask 1, matching accuracy for subtask 2, and a combination of FID and Privacy Preservation Score (PPS) for subtask 3; 37 teams registered, 10 submitted runs and 6 wrote working notes papers.
AI.conclusion: The overview sets out the task setup, datasets, metrics and participant approaches and results, which bear on the trade-off between image fidelity and patient privacy in synthetic medical image generation.

title: Left-Right-Consistent Iterative Stereo Matching via Cross-Injection
comment: Accepted to WACV 2027
summary: State-of-the-art stereo matching models predominantly predict the disparity of only the left (reference) view. However, applications such as per-eye AR/VR rendering, novel view synthesis, or two-view depth fusion require disparity for both views, and need those two maps to agree. The usual workaround of running the network a second time on the horizontally flipped and swapped pair gives two independent predictions that can be inconsistent, especially on transparent surfaces, in textureless regions, and at occlusion boundaries. We introduce cross-injection (CI), a lightweight extension for iterative (refinement-based) models that can be added to any pretrained left-only iterative matcher. It couples the two passes by injecting the explicit, signed left-right inconsistency as an additional input cue at every step of the refinement stage. We empirically show that CI substantially reduces left-right disagreement on every benchmark (more than halving it on Booster for FoundationStereo), while largely preserving sharp object boundaries. Furthermore, using two state-of-the-art stereo matching models, we show that CI also reduces the single-view disparity error, making it a worthwhile extension even if only left disparity is needed.

AI.tldr: Cross-injection (CI) is a lightweight extension for iterative stereo matchers that injects the signed left-right inconsistency at every refinement step, so the two disparity maps agree; it reduces left-right disagreement on every benchmark and also lowers single-view disparity error.
AI.motivation: Stereo models predict only the left disparity, and running the network on the flipped, swapped pair gives two independent predictions that can be inconsistent on transparent surfaces, in textureless regions and at occlusion boundaries, while many applications need both maps to agree.
AI.method: CI can be added to any pretrained left-only iterative matcher and couples the two passes by injecting the explicit, signed left-right inconsistency as an additional input cue at every step of the refinement stage.
AI.result: CI substantially reduces left-right disagreement on every benchmark, more than halving it on Booster for FoundationStereo, while largely preserving sharp object boundaries; with two state-of-the-art stereo models it also reduces single-view disparity error.
AI.conclusion: CI is worthwhile even when only left disparity is needed, because it improves single-view accuracy while making two-view outputs consistent.

title: Embedding Predictive Adaptation and Refinement for Multi-Modal Industrial Anomaly Detection
comment: Accepted to WACV 2027
summary: Industrial Anomaly Detection (IAD) has evolved from 2D image-based approaches to multi-modal methods that leverage the complementary nature of RGB images and 3D point clouds. Among these, memory bank-based methods, which identify anomalies by the discrepancy between each query patch feature and its nearest normal prototype, have proven particularly effective. However, two limitations remain: (i) employing frozen pretrained encoders yields insufficient discrimination between normal and anomalous features due to the domain gap, while existing contrastive learning-based adaptation struggles to capture the spatial relationships required for precise localization; and (ii) pixel-level anomaly maps interpolated from patch-level distance scores remain coarse, lacking fine-grained detail. To address these limitations, we propose EPAR (Embedding Predictive Adaptation and Refinement). We adapt encoders by predicting the embeddings of masked regions to capture spatial relationships, together with patch-level Variance-Invariance-Covariance (VIC) regularization, resolving the poor discriminability between normal and anomalous features caused by the domain gap. We further propose a Noise Suppression Network that refines coarse maps by learning the relational discrepancy between each patch feature and its nearest normal prototype, rather than the anomaly's appearance. This relational signal remains valid for unseen real defects, despite being learned from synthetic anomalies.
