EPAR demonstrates strong practical applicability, excelling in few-shot settings and improving AUPRO@1% on MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies by +1.8% and +1.9%, respectively.

AI.tldr: EPAR (Embedding Predictive Adaptation and Refinement) adapts frozen pretrained encoders for multi-modal industrial anomaly detection through masked-embedding prediction and refines coarse anomaly maps with a Noise Suppression Network, improving AUPRO@1% on MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies by +1.8% and +1.9%.
AI.motivation: Memory-bank methods for RGB and 3D anomaly detection suffer from frozen encoders that give insufficient discrimination because of the domain gap, from contrastive adaptation that struggles to capture the spatial relations needed for precise localization, and from coarse pixel-level maps interpolated from patch-level distances.
AI.method: Encoders are adapted by predicting the embeddings of masked regions together with patch-level Variance-Invariance-Covariance (VIC) regularization; a Noise Suppression Network refines coarse maps by learning the relational discrepancy between each patch feature and its nearest normal prototype, a signal learned from synthetic anomalies.
AI.result: EPAR excels in few-shot settings and improves AUPRO@1% on MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies by +1.8% and +1.9%, respectively.
AI.conclusion: The relational signal learned from synthetic anomalies remains valid for unseen real defects, which gives the approach practical applicability for multi-modal industrial anomaly detection.

title: RadarDINO: Distilling a Visual Foundation Model into mmWave Radar for Human Mesh Reconstruction
summary: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar offers a privacy-preserving and illumination-robust alternative for human mesh reconstruction (HMR). However, high-fidelity radar HMR remains challenging. Sparse point cloud-based methods suffer from information loss and missed detections, while raw radar tensor methods like RT-Mesh lack fine-grained semantics and explicit local body modeling. In this paper, we propose RadarDINO, a radar HMR framework that distills visual semantics from a DINOv3 teacher into 3D radar representations and introduces explicit geometric supervision. DINOv3 descriptors are transferred to radar voxels via calibrated RGB-radar geometry, providing voxel- and body-part-level supervision for part-aware radar representations. We further incorporate vertex- and joint-losses to directly constrain reconstructed geometry. On the M4Human dataset, our method outperforms the SOTA baseline across all three evaluation splits.

AI.tldr: RadarDINO distills DINOv3 visual semantics into mmWave radar voxel representations and adds explicit geometric supervision for human mesh reconstruction, and it outperforms the SOTA baseline across all three evaluation splits of M4Human.
AI.motivation: Millimeter-wave radar offers a privacy-preserving, illumination-robust alternative for human mesh reconstruction, but sparse point cloud methods lose information and miss detections, while raw radar tensor methods such as RT-Mesh lack fine-grained semantics and explicit local body modelling.
AI.method: DINOv3 descriptors from a teacher are transferred to radar voxels through calibrated RGB-radar geometry, giving voxel- and body-part-level supervision for part-aware radar representations, and vertex and joint losses directly constrain the reconstructed geometry.
AI.result: On the M4Human dataset the method outperforms the SOTA baseline across all three evaluation splits.
AI.conclusion: Distilling a visual foundation model into radar, together with explicit geometric supervision, yields part-aware radar representations that improve human mesh reconstruction.

title: ExQuery: Explicit Structured Query Priors for Temporal 3D Object Detection
comment: BMVC 2026
summary: Sparse query-based 3D detectors commonly encode heterogeneous semantic, geometric, and motion information into unified latent queries, including when explicit 3D anchors are used. We introduce ExQuery, an explicit structured query framework for temporal 3D object detection. Each decoded query is organized into a shared semantic context slice and physical-state-specific slices for center, dimensions, orientation, and velocity. This structure is preserved from prior encoding to branch-specific regression and is reused to reconstruct temporal queries: predicted physical states are transformed by ego motion, classification scores form soft semantic priors, and the reconstructed query is fused with the stored latent instance feature through gated affine modulation. Experiments on the nuScenes benchmark show that our method achieves competitive detection performance, and ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our proposed modules.

AI.tldr: ExQuery organizes decoded queries in sparse query-based 3D detection into an explicit shared semantic slice and physical-state slices, then reuses them to build temporal queries through ego-motion transformation and gated affine fusion, achieving competitive detection on nuScenes.
AI.motivation: Sparse query-based 3D detectors encode heterogeneous semantic, geometric and motion information into unified latent queries, even when explicit 3D anchors are used, which obscures the structure needed to reuse queries over time.
AI.method: Each query is organized into a shared semantic context slice and slices for center, dimensions, orientation and velocity; predicted physical states are transformed by ego motion, classification scores form soft semantic priors, and the reconstructed query is fused with the stored latent instance feature through gated affine modulation.
AI.result: Experiments on the nuScenes benchmark show competitive detection performance, and ablation studies validate the proposed modules.
AI.conclusion: Preserving explicit query structure from encoding through branch-specific regression, and reusing it to reconstruct temporal queries, offers a viable design for temporal 3D object detection.

title: Video Stitching from Multiple Moving Cameras
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026
summary: We address geometric video alignment for the same scene captured by multiple freely moving cameras. Existing methods, which are based on image stitching or video stabilization, are typically limited to two cameras or must assume the restrictive setting of a fixed linear ordering of the cameras. We propose MViS, a lightweight test-time optimization framework for joint multi-view alignment with temporal consistency. MViS uses a spatial-transformer-inspired net to jointly process frames from all views within a short temporal window and predict per-view, per-time homographies. Optimization proceeds in two stages: geometry-guided alignment followed by appearance-based refinement, with both stages enforcing multi-view and temporal consistency across the sequence. The method requires no scene-specific hyperparameter tuning, handles arbitrary and time-varying view-intersection graphs, and remains robust under rapid camera motion. On a standard two-view video benchmark, MViS matches or surpasses the state of the art. To facilitate evaluation in more complex scenarios, we introduce an annotated dataset with more than two freely moving cameras and establish the first benchmark for this setting. Project page: this https URL .

AI.tldr: MViS is a lightweight test-time optimization framework that jointly aligns videos from multiple freely moving cameras with temporal consistency, using per-view, per-time homographies; it matches or surpasses the state of the art on a standard two-view benchmark and introduces a benchmark for more than two cameras.
AI.motivation: Existing alignment methods based on image stitching or video stabilization are typically limited to two cameras or must assume a fixed linear ordering of the cameras.
AI.method: A spatial-transformer-inspired network jointly processes frames from all views within a short temporal window to predict per-view, per-time homographies; optimization runs geometry-guided alignment followed by appearance-based refinement, with both stages enforcing multi-view and temporal consistency and no scene-specific hyperparameter tuning.
AI.result: On a standard two-view video benchmark MViS matches or surpasses the state of the art, handles arbitrary and time-varying view-intersection graphs, and remains robust under rapid camera motion.
AI.conclusion: The annotated dataset with more than two freely moving cameras establishes the first benchmark for this setting, which enables evaluation of multi-view video alignment in more complex scenarios.

title: MSR-ABC: Complementary Feature Fusion for Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification
comment: Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027
summary: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) classification from computed tomography (CT) may benefit from representations that capture different aspects of tumour phenotype. However, simply concatenating reconstruction-derived features, image--text embeddings, and radiomic descriptors may not fully exploit their complementary information. We propose MSR-ABC, a global--local framework integrating MedVAE, MedSigLIP, and radiomics. Spatially matched local image descriptors interact through cross-representation attention, while radiomic auxiliary supervision encourages the pooled local representation to retain quantitative tumour attributes. A gated residual mechanism integrates local information with global summaries. Area-aware pooling and visual and soft-text prompting complete the framework. We evaluate discrimination using a patient-level split of 396 KiTS23 cases and an external cohort of 111 TCGA/TCIA cases, reporting mean AUROC over three training seeds with 95% patient-bootstrap confidence intervals. MSR-ABC achieves mean AUROCs of 0.806 internally and 0.879 externally. Internally, it exceeds global MedVAE--radiomics and three-source concatenation by 3.35 and 3.61 AUROC percentage points, respectively. Removing any source lowers mean AUROC in both cohorts, with the largest decreases following radiomics removal. Individual removal of cross-representation attention, auxiliary supervision, or gated fusion also lowers internal mean AUROC. These findings are consistent with complementary contributions within the integrated architecture and support further investigation of structured representation fusion for non-invasive renal tumour characterisation.

AI.tldr: MSR-ABC integrates MedVAE, MedSigLIP and radiomics with cross-representation attention and gated residual fusion for clear cell renal cell carcinoma classification from CT, reaching mean AUROCs of 0.806 internally on 396 KiTS23 cases and 0.879 externally on 111 TCGA/TCIA cases.
AI.motivation: Simply concatenating reconstruction-derived features, image-text embeddings and radiomic descriptors may not fully exploit their complementary information for ccRCC classification.
AI.method: A global-local framework in which spatially matched local image descriptors interact through cross-representation attention, radiomic auxiliary supervision encourages the pooled local representation to keep quantitative tumour attributes, and a gated residual mechanism integrates local information with global summaries, completed by area-aware pooling and visual and soft-text prompting.
AI.result: Mean AUROCs are 0.806 internally and 0.879 externally, averaged over three training seeds with 95% patient-bootstrap confidence intervals; internally it exceeds global MedVAE-radiomics and three-source concatenation by 3.35 and 3.61 AUROC points, and removing any source lowers mean AUROC, with the largest drop after radiomics removal.
AI.conclusion: The results are consistent with complementary contributions from the integrated components and support further investigation of structured representation fusion for non-invasive renal tumour characterisation.

title: Dual-Region Slice Aggregation for CT-Based Renal Tumor Classification
comment: Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027
summary: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most common kidney cancer in adults. We present a region-aware architecture for CT-based ccRCC classification. Tumor and 0--10 mm peritumoral context are pooled separately from shared frozen DINOv3 feature maps. A shared position-aware slice aggregator precedes fixed training-only principal component analysis (PCA). The resulting representations are fused with radiomics using two scalar feature gates. Evaluation on KiTS23 and 111 external cases yields internal test and external AUCs of 0.8078\pm0.0154 and 0.9094\pm0.0015. Compared with matched single-tumor readout, mean AUC increases by 1.50 and 2.34 percentage points, respectively. Early-PCA and reconstruction controls yield lower internal mean AUCs, while external AUC is similar for early and late PCA. These findings highlight the joint role of regional readout and slice aggregation in adapting frozen visual features to renal CT.

AI.tldr: A region-aware architecture pools tumour and 0-10 mm peritumoral context separately from frozen DINOv3 feature maps, fuses them with radiomics through two scalar feature gates, and reaches internal and external AUCs of 0.8078 and 0.9094 for CT-based ccRCC classification.
AI.motivation: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma is the most common kidney cancer in adults, and the work aims to adapt frozen visual features to renal CT for its classification.
AI.method: Tumour and 0-10 mm peritumoral regions are pooled separately from shared frozen DINOv3 feature maps; a shared position-aware slice aggregator precedes fixed training-only principal component analysis (PCA), and the resulting representations are fused with radiomics using two scalar feature gates.
AI.result: Internal test and external AUCs are 0.8078 ± 0.0154 and 0.9094 ± 0.0015; compared with a matched single-tumour readout, mean AUC increases by 1.50 and 2.34 percentage points, and early-PCA and reconstruction controls yield lower internal mean AUCs.
AI.conclusion: The regional readout and slice aggregation jointly help adapt frozen visual features to renal CT, a point the paper highlights through these results.

title: CRTrack-Cap: A New Benchmark for Cross-View Dense Video Object Captioning
summary: Dense video object captioning (DVOC) localizes, tracks, and describes object trajectories within a video. Existing methods process each camera view independently, producing separate camera-local tracklets and captions for the same person across cameras. These outputs lack a unified description and leave complementary appearance evidence across views unused. We therefore formulate cross-view DVOC (CVDVOC), which associates these tracklets into scene-level global trajectories and generates one caption for each trajectory from synchronized views. To support this task, we construct CRTrack-Cap from CRTrack by auditing text-identity links and converting usable referring expressions into canonical captions. It retains 425 global trajectories and 838 local tracklets across 13 scenes, with canonical captions for 335 identities. We adapt CHOTA to the cross-view setting as CV-CHOTA to jointly evaluate tracking and caption quality. Our reference framework combines View-Exclusive Cross-Camera Association (VECA) for grouping tracklets with Conflict-Evidence Gating (CEG) for integrating caption evidence using its reliability and disagreement across views. Against three single-view methods adapted with MvMHAT for cross-view association, our framework achieves CV-CHOTA scores of 83.43 and 33.48 on the scene-disjoint in-domain and cross-domain tests, respectively. Together, CRTrack-Cap and our framework provide a benchmark and a strong baseline for describing the same person consistently across camera views.

AI.tldr: CRTrack-Cap is a benchmark for cross-view dense video object captioning that associates camera-local tracklets into global trajectories with one caption each, and a reference framework reaches CV-CHOTA scores of 83.43 in-domain and 33.48 cross-domain.
AI.motivation: Existing dense video object captioning processes each camera view independently, producing separate tracklets and captions for the same person across cameras and leaving complementary appearance evidence across views unused.
AI.method: The benchmark is built by auditing text-identity links in CRTrack and converting usable referring expressions into canonical captions, and CHOTA is adapted to the cross-view setting as CV-CHOTA; the reference framework combines View-Exclusive Cross-Camera Association (VECA) for grouping tracklets with Conflict-Evidence Gating (CEG) for integrating caption evidence by its reliability and disagreement across views.
AI.result: Against three single-view methods adapted with MvMHAT for cross-view association, the framework achieves CV-CHOTA scores of 83.43 and 33.48 on the scene-disjoint in-domain and cross-domain tests, respectively.
AI.conclusion: CRTrack-Cap and the reference framework provide a benchmark and a strong baseline for describing the same person consistently across camera views, with 425 global trajectories and 838 local tracklets across 13 scenes.

title: Decoupled Mode Connectivity for Base-to-Novel Generalization in Vision-Language Models
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 46 pages (10 main + references, appendix and checklist), 15 figures. Project page: this https URL Code:this https URL
summary: Prompt learning adapts vision-language models such as CLIP by optimizing a short learnable prompt. The cross-entropy objective pulls this prompt toward base-class specialization, whereas generalization to unseen classes benefits from staying close to CLIP's zero-shot feature space. Because both objectives act on the same prompt, their gradients conflict at convergence, and in our experiments no single-prompt loss design clearly improves on the cosine baseline. We propose Decoupled Mode Connectivity (DMC), which gives each objective its own prompt. Starting from a base-trained prompt, DMC trains a specialization prompt and a generalization prompt, and merges their text features with a fixed coefficient at test time, at the inference cost of a single prompt. A linear mode connectivity (LMC) corridor in text-feature space keeps the classification loss low for every classifier interpolated between the two endpoints, and a Visual Anchor KL term preserves CLIP's zero-shot class-similarity distribution of each image during specialization. We further argue that such regularizers should satisfy class-permutation invariance (CPI), and show via Fano's inequality, in an idealized model, that violating CPI lower-bounds the drop in novel accuracy by a term proportional to the mutual information between the prompt and the base-class labels. Across 11 datasets, DMC improves the average harmonic mean of base and novel accuracy over MergeTune for both CoOp and KgCoOp, and its interpolation curves pass beyond the single-prompt operating point, shifting the base-novel frontier rather than trading along it. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: Decoupled Mode Connectivity (DMC) gives the specialization and generalization objectives of CLIP prompt learning their own prompts and merges their text features with a fixed coefficient at test time, improving the average base-novel harmonic mean over MergeTune for both CoOp and KgCoOp across 11 datasets.
AI.motivation: In prompt learning, the cross-entropy objective pulls one shared prompt toward base-class specialization while generalization to unseen classes benefits from staying close to CLIP's zero-shot feature space, so their gradients conflict and no single-prompt loss design clearly improves on the cosine baseline.
AI.method: DMC starts from a base-trained prompt and trains a specialization prompt and a generalization prompt; a linear mode connectivity corridor in text-feature space keeps the classification loss low for every interpolated classifier, a Visual Anchor KL term preserves CLIP's zero-shot class-similarity distribution during specialization, and class-permutation invariance is argued through Fano's inequality in an idealized model.
AI.result: Across 11 datasets DMC improves the average harmonic mean of base and novel accuracy over MergeTune for both CoOp and KgCoOp, and its interpolation curves pass beyond the single-prompt operating point.
AI.conclusion: The gains shift the base-novel frontier rather than trading accuracy along it, and the paper argues that violating class-permutation invariance lower-bounds the drop in novel accuracy by a term proportional to the mutual information between the prompt and the base-class labels.

title: Video2Asset: Online Construction of Persistent 3D Street-Scene Assets
summary: Online 3D street-scene asset construction turns multi-view video into a continually updated scene of independently editable objects. The central challenge is to accumulate partial, intermittent observations under motion and occlusion without fragmenting identities or mixing evidence across objects. To address this challenge, we propose Video2Asset, an online framework for constructing persistent 3D assets from multi-view video. Using occupancy as an intermediate representation, we construct identity-aware observations with Historical Carrier Guidance for instance decoding and an identity encoder fusing instance-aligned 3D features with multi-view appearance. Accumulated-Evidence Association compares current observations with identity, geometric, and appearance evidence accumulated within asset records to determine identity inheritance and update world-coordinate states. We instantiate meshes from an asset library using these states and combine them with an occupancy-derived static background to support scene visualization, mesh replacement, object deletion, and trajectory editing. Experiments on several datasets demonstrate improvements in temporal identity consistency and asset quality across multiple occupancy models, including a 15.4% reduction in asset fragmentation on nuScenes with SGE.

AI.tldr: Video2Asset is an online framework that builds persistent, independently editable 3D street-scene assets from multi-view video, using occupancy as an intermediate representation and accumulated evidence for identity association, and it reports a 15.4% reduction in asset fragmentation on nuScenes with SGE.
AI.motivation: Accumulating partial, intermittent observations under motion and occlusion, without fragmenting identities or mixing evidence across objects, is the central challenge of online 3D street-scene asset construction.
AI.method: Identity-aware observations come from Historical Carrier Guidance for instance decoding and an identity encoder that fuses instance-aligned 3D features with multi-view appearance; Accumulated-Evidence Association compares current observations with identity, geometric and appearance evidence stored in asset records to decide identity inheritance and update world-coordinate states, and meshes are instantiated from an asset library.
AI.result: Experiments on several datasets show improved temporal identity consistency and asset quality across multiple occupancy models, including a 15.4% reduction in asset fragmentation on nuScenes with SGE.
AI.conclusion: The framework supports scene visualization, mesh replacement, object deletion and trajectory editing on top of an occupancy-derived static background.

title: Dual Architecture Fusion Vehicle Lidar 3D Target Detection
comment: 5 pages, 6 figures. Published in CAIBDA 2026
summary: In this paper, a 3D backbone network (SpconvTransformer) based on the fusion of convolutional architecture branch and Transformer architecture branch is proposed. The convolution branch uses 3D sparse convolution and submanifold convolution to learn local voxel features and semantic information, and the Transformer branch uses the self-attention mechanism to model the remote relationship between voxels, uses the broad receptive field to capture rich context information, and complementing the advantages of the two architectures by fusing the local features extracted from the two branches and the global features solves the problem of limited receptive fields of 3D convolutional neural networks. The experimental results show that the average accuracy of SpconvTransformer in 3D object detection and bird's-eye view detection tasks reaches 81.45% and 88.09%, respectively, and the average directional similarity reaches 91.10%, which is significantly better than other existing algorithms.

AI.tldr: SpconvTransformer fuses a 3D sparse convolution branch with a Transformer self-attention branch as a backbone for vehicle LiDAR 3D object detection, reaching 81.45% average accuracy in 3D detection and 88.09% in bird's-eye-view detection.
AI.motivation: The limited receptive field of 3D convolutional networks restricts context, so local voxel features need to be complemented with long-range relations between voxels.
AI.method: A convolution branch with 3D sparse and submanifold convolutions learns local voxel features and semantic information, a Transformer branch uses self-attention to model long-range relations between voxels, and the local features from both branches are fused with global features.
AI.result: Average accuracy reaches 81.45% for 3D object detection and 88.09% for bird's-eye-view detection, and average directional similarity reaches 91.10%, which the paper reports as significantly better than other existing algorithms.
AI.conclusion: Combining local convolutional and global Transformer features addresses the receptive-field limitation of 3D convolutional networks in LiDAR detection.

title: PoseRieFlow: Riemannian Flow Matching for Whole-Body Text-to-Pose Generation
summary: We present PoseRieFlow, a compact flow-matching framework for text-conditioned generation of whole-body 3D human poses. Prior text-to-pose methods either neglect articulated hands or model rotations in Euclidean space despite their non-Euclidean geometry. PoseRieFlow instead formulates generation directly on the product manifold of SMPL-H joint rotations, learning a text-conditioned vector field that transports samples from an isotropic $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ Gaussian prior to the data distribution along Riemannian geodesics. A part-tokenized Diffusion Transformer aggregates the 52 joints into eight body-part tokens, allocating a dedicated token and nonlinear projector to each hand, and restores per-joint resolution through part-specific decoders, shortening the sequence while improving kinematic fidelity over per-joint tokenization. With only 21.6M trainable parameters, PoseRieFlow supports expressive SMPL-H generation with detailed hand articulation at a fraction of the scale of recent LLM-based generators. On PoseScript, it attains the lowest whole-body kinematic error among all hand-producing methods, with consistent kinematic gains from the Riemannian formulation over its Euclidean counterpart at every practical inference budget, while distributional and retrieval metrics remain comparable between them.

AI.tldr: PoseRieFlow is a compact flow-matching model that generates whole-body SMPL-H human poses from text by working on the product manifold of joint rotations and grouping the 52 joints into eight body-part tokens; with 21.6M trainable parameters it attains the lowest whole-body kinematic error among hand-producing methods on PoseScript.
AI.motivation: Prior text-to-pose methods either neglect articulated hands or model rotations in Euclidean space despite their non-Euclidean geometry.
AI.method: Riemannian flow matching transports samples from an isotropic SO(3) Gaussian prior to the data distribution along geodesics on the product manifold of SMPL-H joint rotations; a part-tokenized Diffusion Transformer aggregates the 52 joints into eight body-part tokens with a dedicated token and nonlinear projector for each hand, and part-specific decoders restore per-joint resolution.
AI.result: On PoseScript the model attains the lowest whole-body kinematic error among all hand-producing methods, and the Riemannian formulation gives consistent kinematic gains over its Euclidean counterpart at every practical inference budget, while distributional and retrieval metrics remain comparable.
AI.conclusion: Riemannian formulation and part-based tokenization give expressive whole-body generation with detailed hand articulation at a fraction of the scale of recent LLM-based generators.

title: Direct Regression and Geometric Recovery for Event-based Spacecraft Pose Estimation
summary: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and dynamic range for uncooperative spacecraft pose estimation, but models trained on synthetic event streams must generalize to the noise, background activity, and contrast variation of physical sensors. We present a comparative systems study of two independently developed approaches to synthetic-to-real, event-based 6-DoF spacecraft pose estimation. The first is a modular pipeline that combines learned keypoint detection and unlabeled target-domain adaptation with geometry-based pose recovery and temporal smoothing. The second directly regresses translation and rotation from global and cropped event representations using an apparent-scale cue, physics-motivated synthetic corruptions, and feature-consistency regularization. We evaluate both systems under the same SPARK 2026 hidden-test protocol on the real-event split of SPADES, with predictions for all test frames. The results reveal a component-wise reversal concealed by the aggregate challenge score: direct regression reduces orientation error by 22.7% (1.1767 to 0.9101 rad) and obtains a 13.4% lower composite score, whereas the modular pipeline reduces relative translation error by 78.7% (0.1335 to 0.0285). Archived configurations and a qualitative failure case identify plausible explanations for these complementary error profiles, without isolating their causes. These findings motivate a testable hybrid design that combines direct orientation estimation with geometry-constrained translation recovery.

AI.tldr: A comparative systems study of two independently developed synthetic-to-real event-based 6-DoF spacecraft pose estimators finds that direct regression cuts orientation error by 22.7% while a modular geometric pipeline cuts relative translation error by 78.7%, a component-wise reversal hidden by the aggregate challenge score.
AI.motivation: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and dynamic range for uncooperative spacecraft pose estimation, but models trained on synthetic event streams must generalize to the noise, background activity and contrast variation of physical sensors.
AI.method: One system is a modular pipeline of learned keypoint detection, unlabeled target-domain adaptation, geometry-based pose recovery and temporal smoothing; the other regresses translation and rotation directly from global and cropped event representations using an apparent-scale cue, physics-motivated synthetic corruptions and feature-consistency regularization; both are evaluated under the SPARK 2026 hidden-test protocol on the real-event split of SPADES.
AI.result: Direct regression reduces orientation error by 22.7% (1.1767 to 0.9101 rad) and obtains a 13.4% lower composite score, whereas the modular pipeline reduces relative translation error by 78.7% (0.1335 to 0.0285).
AI.conclusion: The complementary error profiles motivate a testable hybrid design that combines direct orientation estimation with geometry-constrained translation recovery, although the causes of the profiles are not isolated.

title: Evaluating Anterior Cruciate Ligament Risk of Injury Using a Graph Convolutional Autoencoder
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures
summary: Current solutions for assessing the risk of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury typically rely on expensive motion-capture labs that require substantial resource investment or subjective evaluations of specific athletic stress tests by experts. The Drop Vertical Jump (DVJ) and the Single Leg Hop (SLH) are two examples of such tests typically used to track progress in ACL rehabilitation. In this paper, we develop an unsupervised learning model that runs entirely on a smartphone for two tasks, based on an autoencoder architecture with multiple layers of graph convolutional networks, which utilizes pose estimation data to determine a person's injury risk status. Our model accurately predicts athletes at high risk of injury for both athletic stress tests, with average sensitivities and specificities of 78% and 78% for the DVJ, and 75% and 74% for the SLH. Our findings support the development of a widely accessible smartphone solution for real-time screening of ACL injury risk.

AI.tldr: An unsupervised graph convolutional autoencoder that runs entirely on a smartphone uses pose estimation data to flag athletes at high ACL injury risk in the drop vertical jump (DVJ) and single leg hop (SLH) tests, with average sensitivities and specificities of 78% and 78% for the DVJ and 75% and 74% for the SLH.
AI.motivation: Assessing ACL injury risk typically relies on expensive motion-capture labs or on subjective expert evaluation of athletic stress tests.
AI.method: An autoencoder with multiple layers of graph convolutional networks, trained without labels, takes pose estimation data from the DVJ and SLH tests to determine each person's injury risk status.
AI.result: The model accurately predicts athletes at high risk of injury on both tests, with average sensitivities and specificities of 78% and 78% for the DVJ and 75% and 74% for the SLH.
AI.conclusion: The findings support the development of a widely accessible smartphone solution for real-time screening of ACL injury risk.

title: TriNetra: Thermal-Reliability-Guided RGB-Thermal Fusion and Tracking for Surveillance
summary: Visible cameras fail at night and thermal sensors fail under saturation, blur or loss of contrast, yet most RGB-thermal (RGB-T) detectors mix the two streams with fixed weights and cannot tell when one modality has become unreliable. TriNetra is a reliability-aware surveillance framework built around this problem. The proposed solution computes a frame-level Thermal Reliability Coefficient (TRC) from five label-free image cues, uses it to gate the thermal features of a dual-branch YOLOv8m detector whose visible branch, neck and head are frozen and COCO-pretrained, and passes the same score to a ByteTrack-based tracker that feeds a rule-based behaviour analyser. On the M3FD benchmark (2,940/630/630 split) the detector reaches 87.6% precision, 79.4% recall, 70.0% mAP@50 and 47.8% mAP@50:95 on the test split, with 17.0 M of its 42.9 M parameters trained. TRC stays near 0.78 on clean frames (standard deviation 0.012), decreases with the severity of thermal saturation and blur, reaching 0.53 and 0.69 at full severity, and is insensitive to RGB-thermal misalignment. With identical weights, the adaptive gate matches a fixed gate on clean data (70.0% versus 69.8% mAP@50) but keeps 43.6% mAP@50 when the thermal stream is corrupted, against 38.4%, 29.2% and 25.0% for a fixed gate, full thermal admission and a closed gate; the 5.1-point gain over the fixed gate has a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of +3.6 to +6.5 points. In tracking, the TRC-gated association performs on par with ByteTrack on a synthetic benchmark with exact ground truth and on 14 M3FD clips, and is slightly less stable under thermal saturation, so its measured benefit is confined to the detector. The limitations of the current evaluation are reported together with the results.

AI.tldr: TriNetra is a reliability-aware RGB-thermal surveillance framework whose Thermal Reliability Coefficient (TRC) gates the thermal features of a YOLOv8m detector and feeds a ByteTrack-based tracker; on M3FD it reaches 70.0% mAP@50 and keeps 43.6% mAP@50 when the thermal stream is corrupted.
AI.motivation: Most RGB-thermal detectors mix the two streams with fixed weights and cannot tell when one modality has become unreliable, for example visible cameras at night or thermal sensors under saturation, blur or loss of contrast.
AI.method: A frame-level TRC is computed from five label-free image cues and used to gate the thermal features of a dual-branch YOLOv8m detector whose visible branch, neck and head are frozen and COCO-pretrained; the same score is passed to a ByteTrack-based tracker that feeds a rule-based behaviour analyser.
AI.result: On M3FD the detector reaches 87.6% precision, 79.4% recall, 70.0% mAP@50 and 47.8% mAP@50:95; with corrupted thermal input the adaptive gate keeps 43.6% mAP@50, against 38.4%, 29.2% and 25.0% for a fixed gate, full thermal admission and a closed gate, and the 5.1-point gain over the fixed gate has a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of +3.6 to +6.5 points.
AI.conclusion: The measured benefit is confined to the detector, since TRC-gated association performs on par with ByteTrack and is slightly less stable under thermal saturation, and the limitations of the current evaluation are reported with the results.

title: Zero-Shot Benchmarking of Unified Multimodal Models for Shallow-Water UAV Image Distortion Assessment and Restoration
summary: Shallow-water UAV imagery provides centimeter-scale observations of benthic environments, but water-induced distortions complicate interpretation. To our knowledge, we present the first systematic zero-shot benchmark of unified multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for both assessing water-induced distortions and restoring shallow-water imagery within the same model framework. We evaluate five open-weight unified MLLMs with frozen pretrained weights and without access to paired reference images or descriptions of the true seabed. The benchmark contains 1,000 image pairs: 600 semi-synthetic UAV scenes created by applying synthetic water distortions to real shallow-water imagery and 400 fully synthetic through-water scenes. Three independent human annotations cover five distortion types. We evaluate four assessment prompts (P0-P3), from direct instruction to structured task decomposition, on all 1,000 images and four diagnosis-guided restoration prompts (R0-R3) on a common 100-image subset. Assessment varies substantially by model and prompt, with systematic prediction biases and a best pooled balanced accuracy of 0.654 for distortion presence. The best pooled PSNR gain is +0.255 dB, no unified MLLM improves pooled LPIPS, and some outputs alter scene structure or hallucinate content. Two restoration-only baselines also show limited transfer: InstructIR achieves a pooled PSNR gain of +0.040 dB, while PromptFix degrades all four pooled metrics under every prompt. These results show that recognizing shallow-water degradation does not imply reliable physical restoration and provide a reproducible baseline for future work.

AI.tldr: A zero-shot benchmark of five open-weight unified multimodal LLMs on 1,000 shallow-water UAV image pairs finds that recognizing water-induced distortion does not imply reliable physical restoration; the best pooled balanced accuracy for distortion presence is 0.654 and the best pooled PSNR gain is +0.255 dB.
AI.motivation: Water-induced distortions complicate the interpretation of shallow-water UAV imagery, and no systematic benchmark had tested unified multimodal LLMs on both assessing and restoring such imagery within one framework.
AI.method: Five frozen open-weight unified MLLMs are evaluated without paired reference images or seabed descriptions on 1,000 pairs (600 semi-synthetic and 400 fully synthetic) with three human annotations covering five distortion types, using four assessment prompts (P0-P3) on all images and four diagnosis-guided restoration prompts (R0-R3) on a 100-image subset, with two restoration-only baselines, InstructIR and PromptFix.
AI.result: Assessment varies substantially by model and prompt, with systematic prediction biases and a best pooled balanced accuracy of 0.654 for distortion presence; no unified MLLM improves pooled LPIPS, some outputs alter scene structure or hallucinate content, InstructIR gains +0.040 dB in pooled PSNR, and PromptFix degrades all four pooled metrics under every prompt.
AI.conclusion: Recognizing shallow-water degradation does not imply reliable physical restoration, and the benchmark provides a reproducible baseline for future work.

title: A lightweight convolutional neural network for target detection in an edge environment
comment: Presented at GVSETS 2023, Novi, MI. Distribution A: approved for public release
summary: This paper proposes a novel, lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) designed for edge device deployment. The CNN is developed to recognize and classify threats or targets of interest. The model is equipped with a real-time hotspot detection algorithm, which enables it to process information quickly and accurately, resulting in improved inference time of up to 20 fps and a detection range of more than 400 meters with typical thermal situational awareness sensors. The proposed CNN has been rigorously tested and validated to demonstrate its high accuracy, sensitivity, and low false positive rate, providing a reliable solution for edge devices to detect potential targets. Additionally, the lightweight design of the CNN allows for easy deployment, making it an ideal solution for extending the security bubble for edge devices. The proposed model can be used for a variety of applications, including surveillance, security, and object recognition.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a lightweight CNN for edge devices that recognizes and classifies targets in thermal imagery, using a real-time hotspot detection algorithm. It reports inference up to 20 fps and detection beyond 400 meters with typical thermal situational awareness sensors.
AI.motivation: Edge devices need target detection that is accurate, fast and easy to deploy, and the abstract presents the lightweight design as the way to extend the security bubble for such devices.
AI.method: A novel lightweight convolutional neural network combined with a real-time hotspot detection algorithm, designed for edge deployment with thermal sensors.
AI.result: Inference up to 20 fps and a detection range of more than 400 meters with typical thermal sensors, with high accuracy, sensitivity and low false positive rate reported after testing and validation; the abstract gives no specific accuracy figures.
AI.conclusion: The model is presented as a reliable edge solution for detecting potential targets, applicable to surveillance, security and object recognition.

title: AR-Edit: Training-Free Autoregressive Video Editing without Inversion
summary: Editing a video stream in real time, without access to future frames, is essential for interactive applications. Existing training-free video editing methods, however, assume full offline access to the entire sequence, while streaming approaches either rely on additional training or are limited to specific editing techniques. We show that this limitation can be removed by analyzing the self-attention dynamics of DMD-distilled autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models. We uncover a key asymmetry: queries and keys remain stable and aligned with their source counterparts across denoising timesteps, while values diverge and encode the evolving content. Inherited from the non-distilled bidirectional teacher, this asymmetry is strongest at high noise, where few-step streaming models operate. The resulting mechanism is simple: a single forward pass suffices to capture source identity in the value features, which can be reused throughout generation. Starting from pure Gaussian noise and injecting only these source values reconstructs the input with fidelity matching or surpassing inversion-based methods, effectively eliminating inversion. Based on this insight, we introduce AR-Edit, a training-free, inversion-free method that caches source values once and selectively injects them during denoising. Across multiple AR backbones, AR-Edit enables real-time streaming editing with superior source preservation and tonal fidelity at minimal overhead.

AI.tldr: AR-Edit performs training-free, inversion-free streaming video editing with DMD-distilled autoregressive video diffusion models by caching source values once and injecting them during denoising. It reports source preservation and tonal fidelity superior to inversion-based methods at minimal overhead.
AI.motivation: Existing training-free video editing methods assume offline access to the whole sequence, while streaming approaches either need additional training or support only specific editing techniques.
AI.method: Analysis of self-attention dynamics shows that queries and keys stay aligned with their source counterparts across denoising steps while values diverge and encode evolving content, most strongly at high noise. A single forward pass captures source identity in the value features, which are cached and selectively injected from pure Gaussian noise.
AI.result: Reconstruction fidelity matching or surpassing inversion-based methods across multiple AR backbones, with real-time streaming editing, superior source preservation and tonal fidelity, and minimal overhead.
AI.conclusion: Inversion can be removed from streaming video editing with autoregressive diffusion models, enabling real-time interactive editing without training.

title: BEV3SR: Evidence-Aware 3D Spatial Reasoning from Video
comment: WACV camera ready
summary: 3D spatial reasoning from video remains challenging for VLMs because videos provide sequential, view-local observations rather than persistent metric scene records. Many questions must be answered in a query-specified perspective rather than the observed camera viewpoint, and prompting with a fixed set of RGB views may miss sparse or occluded visual cues. To address these gaps, we introduce BEV3SR, a training-free and backbone-agnostic framework for RGB-D videos with camera parameters. BEV3SR turns video observations into queryable metric bird's-eye-view (BEV) scene memory and formalizes each query into an evidence-aware spatial task. The Spatial Task Formalizer specifies the query's reference frame, spatial constraints, objective, and evidence requirement. The evidence requirement determines the appropriate reasoning pathway. A query treated as requiring geometric evidence is handled by the Geometric Reasoner, which deterministically computes the answer using the metric BEV records in the query-specified reference frame. Otherwise, a query treated as requiring visual evidence is passed to the Visual Evidence Aligner, which uses BEV-indexed object records and their associated supporting views to retrieve object-consistent and scene-context RGB frames for VLM grounding. Within a standard 16-frame budget, BEV3SR consistently improves different VLM backbones across multiple 3D scene QA benchmarks, delivering large gains on spatially intensive questions and significant improvements on open-ended scene QA. These results demonstrate that BEV3SR offers an effective, efficient, and interpretable framework for explicit 3D spatial reasoning from video.

AI.tldr: BEV3SR is a training-free, backbone-agnostic framework for 3D spatial reasoning over RGB-D videos that builds a metric bird's-eye-view scene memory and routes each query to geometric or visual evidence reasoning. It consistently improves several VLM backbones on 3D scene QA benchmarks within a 16-frame budget.
AI.motivation: VLMs struggle with 3D spatial reasoning from video because videos give sequential, view-local observations, queries often require a non-camera perspective, and a fixed set of RGB views may miss sparse or occluded cues.
AI.method: Video observations are turned into queryable metric BEV scene memory. A Spatial Task Formalizer specifies reference frame, spatial constraints, objective and evidence requirement. Queries needing geometric evidence go to a Geometric Reasoner that computes answers from BEV records; queries needing visual evidence go to a Visual Evidence Aligner that retrieves object-consistent and scene-context RGB frames for VLM grounding.
AI.result: Consistent improvements across different VLM backbones on multiple 3D scene QA benchmarks, with large gains on spatially intensive questions and significant improvements on open-ended scene QA, within a standard 16-frame budget.
AI.conclusion: The framework is presented as an effective, efficient and interpretable approach to explicit 3D spatial reasoning from video.

title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
comment: 35 pages, 4 main figures, 2 supplementary figures, and 10 supplementary tables. Interactive Results Atlas and Hypothesis Explorer accompany the manuscript
summary: The extent to which demographic-associated information is detectable across organs and disease states in routine clinical histopathology remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 1.3 million hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images from 257,322 patients across 25 organs, using pathology foundation-model representations and multiple-instance learning to systematically map information associated with sex, age group, and self-reported race. Across 69 organ-demographic combinations, demographic attributes were broadly recoverable, with pan-organ mean AUROCs of 0.828 for sex, 0.733 for age group, and 0.662 for self-reported race, and substantial variation across organs. Demographic-class balancing produced relatively small changes in performance, while evaluation within diagnosis-text clusters showed modest attenuation. Under training with diagnosis-based grouping, demographic-associated signals remained detectable across multiple organs, including sex in gastric tissue (AUROC 0.865), age group in breast (0.816), and self-reported race in skin (0.728). Literature-guided analysis of these settings generated candidate histomorphological and contextual explanations for further investigation. Together, these findings provide a systematic map of demographic-associated information in routine histopathology, informing investigations of its sources, assessments of potential shortcut learning, and the development of more interpretable computational pathology models.

AI.tldr: Using pathology foundation-model representations and multiple-instance learning on 1.3 million H&E whole-slide images from 257,322 patients across 25 organs, the study maps how well sex, age group and self-reported race can be recovered from routine histopathology. Demographic attributes are broadly recoverable, with pan-organ mean AUROCs of 0.828 for sex, 0.733 for age group and 0.662 for self-reported race.
AI.motivation: It was unclear how much demographic-associated information is detectable across organs and disease states in routine clinical histopathology, which bears on shortcut learning and the interpretability of computational pathology models.
AI.method: Foundation-model features with multiple-instance learning across 69 organ-demographic combinations, with demographic-class balancing, evaluation within diagnosis-text clusters, diagnosis-based grouping, and literature-guided analysis of candidate histomorphological and contextual explanations.
AI.result: Pan-organ mean AUROCs of 0.828 for sex, 0.733 for age group and 0.662 for self-reported race, with substantial variation across organs. Class balancing changed performance relatively little and diagnosis-cluster evaluation attenuated it modestly. Under diagnosis-based grouping, sex in gastric tissue reached AUROC 0.865, age group in breast 0.816 and self-reported race in skin 0.728.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a systematic map of demographic-associated information in routine histopathology, to inform investigations of its sources, assessments of potential shortcut learning and the development of more interpretable pathology models.

title: Graded convolutional networks: scale invariance without the scale and robustness to unknown blur
comment: 26 pages, 2 figures, 7 tables. Code, trained networks and results: this https URL
summary: The Gaussian jet of an image is a graded vector space: a dilation by $\lambda$ multiplies derivatives of order $k$ by $\lambda^{-k}$. Local graded convolutions are exactly homogeneous differential operators, and a local feature is dilation-invariant if and only if it factors through the scale-normalized jet or, without the scale, through the retraction onto the weighted sphere of the grading. Under unknown Gaussian blur the retraction changes only by a change of scale, whereas the scale-normalized jet acquires a grading factor that no radial normalization removes. At the zero jet the retraction separates image families that radial normalizations and continuous classifiers cannot. Networks built on the retraction are universal for invariant features. On MNIST such a network keeps 88.4% accuracy under a two-pixel blur, against 66.2% for the same network on scale-normalized derivatives; in Lindeberg's Gaussian derivative network the retraction raises accuracy at that blur from 91.5% to 95.1%.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that dilation invariance can be obtained without explicit scale normalization by building networks on a retraction of the image's Gaussian jet onto the weighted sphere of the grading, which improves robustness to unknown blur. On MNIST under two-pixel blur, the retraction-based network keeps 88.4% accuracy versus 66.2% for scale-normalized derivatives.
AI.motivation: Scale-normalized derivatives lose invariance under unknown Gaussian blur because the grading factor is not removed by radial normalization, and radial normalizations and continuous classifiers cannot separate certain image families at the zero jet.
AI.method: Treating the Gaussian jet as a graded vector space, local graded convolutions are exactly homogeneous differential operators. A dilation-invariant feature factors either through the scale-normalized jet or, without the scale, through the retraction onto the weighted sphere; networks are built on the retraction and are universal for invariant features.
AI.result: On MNIST under two-pixel blur, 88.4% accuracy against 66.2% for the same network on scale-normalized derivatives. In Lindeberg's Gaussian derivative network, the retraction raises accuracy at that blur from 91.5% to 95.1%.
AI.conclusion: Retraction-based networks give invariant features that are more robust to unknown blur than scale-normalized alternatives, with the scale itself no longer needed.

title: ZeoBench: A Benchmark for Self-Supervised Learning on 3D Zeolite Representations
comment: NeurIPS 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks Track
summary: Zeolites are an important class of porous crystalline materials with broad applications in gas storage, separations, and catalysis. Although hundreds of thousands of experimentally realized and hypothetical zeolite structures are known, identifying materials optimized for a target application remains challenging because property labels are expensive to obtain and available only for limited structure-molecule pairs. While prior work has demonstrated that 3D neural representations can predict zeolite properties effectively, it remains unclear which representation-learning strategies are most effective in the low-data regime relevant to materials discovery. We present ZeoBench, a benchmark for self-supervised learning on dense 3D representations of all-silica zeolites, and evaluate the resulting features on six existing downstream adsorption-property prediction tasks, across a range of training set sizes. Our study compares self-supervised 3D pretraining on volumetric zeolite data, adaptations of image-pretrained 2D ConvNets and vision transformers to 3D via multiview and channel-inflation strategies, and 3D ConvNets pretrained on out-of-domain volumetric datasets, alongside hand-crafted descriptors and supervised baselines. Using our pretraining and evaluation framework, we find self-supervised 3D representations outperform existing methods and achieve state-of-the-art performance across both in-domain label regimes and for the unseen domain of metal organic frameworks. Learned representations consistently outperform hand-crafted descriptors, and convolutional architectures are generally more effective than vision transformers in this setting. These results establish ZeoBench as a practical benchmark for 3D representation learning in zeolites and provide guidance for data-limited adsorption property prediction.

AI.tldr: ZeoBench is a benchmark for self-supervised learning on dense 3D representations of all-silica zeolites, evaluated on six adsorption-property prediction tasks across training set sizes. Self-supervised 3D representations outperform existing methods and reach state-of-the-art performance in-domain and on metal organic frameworks.
AI.motivation: Property labels for zeolites are expensive and available only for limited structure-molecule pairs, and it was unclear which representation-learning strategies work best in the low-data regime relevant to materials discovery.
AI.method: Compares self-supervised 3D pretraining on volumetric zeolite data, image-pretrained 2D ConvNets and vision transformers adapted to 3D via multiview and channel-inflation strategies, 3D ConvNets pretrained on out-of-domain volumetric datasets, hand-crafted descriptors and supervised baselines.
AI.result: Self-supervised 3D representations outperform existing methods and achieve state-of-the-art performance across in-domain label regimes and for the unseen metal organic framework domain. Learned representations consistently outperform hand-crafted descriptors, and convolutional architectures are generally more effective than vision transformers.
AI.conclusion: ZeoBench establishes a practical benchmark for 3D representation learning in zeolites and gives guidance for data-limited adsorption property prediction.

title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 22 pages, including references and appendix
summary: Predicting the future motion of multiple people is inherently stochastic: the same observed history admits many plausible continuations depending on intent, coordination, and social context. Yet the dominant paradigm in multi-person 3D motion prediction remains deterministic, with existing methods producing a fixed number of outputs per agent. In contrast, we present a conditional flow matching framework that jointly generates diverse future motions for multiple agents, modeling both global trajectories and root-relative poses. A B-spline reparameterization compresses the generative state space while enforcing temporal smoothness, and a dual-stream transformer conditions each agent's predictions on observed neighbor motion for interaction-aware forecasting. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on CMU-Mocap (UMPM) and 3DPW, outperforming deterministic baselines on joint position error, pose error, and final displacement error despite producing a full predictive distribution. We additionally establish the first motion prediction baseline on WorldPose, a large-scale professional soccer dataset, where social conditioning demonstrably concentrates predictive uncertainty along interaction-constrained directions.

AI.tldr: FlowMoP is a conditional flow matching framework that jointly generates diverse, interaction-aware future motions for multiple people. It achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on CMU-Mocap (UMPM) and 3DPW while producing a full predictive distribution.
AI.motivation: Future motion of multiple people is inherently stochastic, yet the dominant paradigm in multi-person 3D motion prediction is deterministic, with a fixed number of outputs per agent.
AI.method: Conditional flow matching jointly generates global trajectories and root-relative poses for multiple agents. A B-spline reparameterization compresses the generative state space while enforcing temporal smoothness, and a dual-stream transformer conditions each agent's predictions on observed neighbor motion.
AI.result: State-of-the-art on CMU-Mocap (UMPM) and 3DPW, outperforming deterministic baselines on joint position error, pose error and final displacement error. The paper also sets the first motion prediction baseline on WorldPose, a large-scale professional soccer dataset, where social conditioning concentrates uncertainty along interaction-constrained directions.
AI.conclusion: Modeling multi-person futures as a distribution improves prediction over deterministic baselines and reveals how social context shapes predictive uncertainty.

title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
comment: Project Page:this https URL Code: this https URL
summary: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in video generation in terms of visual quality and temporal consistency. However, generating videos with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce Video-Coder, the first attempt to train a code-driven video generation agent, which autonomously writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D scene (Draft Video) that provides structure and motion signals to downstream video generators. To support this paradigm, we design a dedicated data pipeline and curate two high-quality datasets, Video-Coder-SFT-6k and Video-Coder-RL-2k, which contain diverse prompts and ground-truth reference videos. We further develop the Video- Coder Harness, a unified interactive environment integrating code execution, 3D scene rendering, and execution feedback for agent training and inference. We then train Video-Coder with SFT fol- lowed by harness-native agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback, which combines execution-based and video-based rewards. Additionally, we design an annealing training strategy that gradually reduces the execution reward over time, allowing the model to rely more on the video reward in the later training stages. Experiments show that Video-Coder achieves significant gains, improving Minimax-H3 by approximately 7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 points on VBench-2.0. We hope this work can serve as an open foundation for coding agents in video generation, and we fully open-source our data, models, and code

AI.tldr: Video-Coder trains an agent that autonomously writes and executes code to build a dynamic 3D scene, the Draft Video, which supplies structure and motion signals to downstream video generators. It improves Minimax-H3 by approximately 7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 points on VBench-2.0.
AI.motivation: Video generation still struggles with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics and controllable scene composition.
AI.method: A code-driven generation agent trained with SFT on Video-Coder-SFT-6k, then harness-native agentic reinforcement learning on Video-Coder-RL-2k using dual rewards that combine execution-based and video-based feedback. An annealing strategy gradually reduces the execution reward, and a unified harness integrates code execution, 3D scene rendering and feedback.
AI.result: Gains of approximately 7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 points on VBench-2.0 for Minimax-H3.
AI.conclusion: The work is offered as an open foundation for coding agents in video generation, with data, models and code released.

title: Deep-Learning Algorithm for Indeterminate Thyroid Nodules: Comparison and Combination with Molecular Testing
comment: 16 pages, 7 figures, 8 tables (3 supplementary)
summary: Thyroid nodules with indeterminate cytology (Bethesda III) carry an intermediate risk of malignancy, and molecular testing is widely used to decide between surgery and surveillance, but it is costly and not universally available. We investigated whether a convolutional neural network (CNN) applied to routine ultrasound images can stratify Bethesda III nodules, and how it compares and combines with molecular testing. We retrospectively identified 466 nodule records from 418 patients who underwent molecular testing (Afirma or ThyroSeq). A CNN pre-trained on determinate nodules was adapted to indeterminate nodules with soft labels and transfer learning. After removal of duplicate records, 119 nodules with surgical pathology were used for development and 47 were held out for testing. On the test set, the deep learning (DL) model achieved an AUC of 0.73 (95% CI 0.51-0.94), compared with 0.55 (0.38-0.71) for molecular testing (P = 0.15). At a cut-off inherited from the original algorithm, the DL model was more specific than molecular testing (0.95 vs 0.32; P < 0.001), with a higher positive predictive value (0.67 vs 0.21), a lower sensitivity (0.44 vs 0.78; P = 0.25) and a similar negative predictive value (0.88 vs 0.86). All six DL-positive test nodules were molecular-positive, and the DL output split the molecular-positive nodules into a high-risk (4/6 malignant) and a lower-risk group (3/27 malignant; P = 0.01). Surgical verification was strongly driven by the molecular result (99% of positive vs 19% of negative results), and molecular-test accuracy depended on the platform. A logistic regression of the DL output, nodule size and the molecular result dropped the DL term and did not improve on the DL output alone. Ultrasound DL complemented molecular testing for Bethesda III nodules, in particular by identifying molecular-positive nodules at lower risk of malignancy.

AI.tldr: A CNN applied to routine ultrasound images stratifies indeterminate (Bethesda III) thyroid nodules and complements molecular testing, mainly by identifying molecular-positive nodules at lower malignancy risk. On the 47-nodule held-out test set its AUC was 0.73, versus 0.55 for molecular testing (P = 0.15).
AI.motivation: Bethesda III nodules carry an intermediate risk of malignancy, and molecular testing used to decide between surgery and surveillance is costly and not universally available.
AI.method: A CNN pre-trained on determinate nodules was adapted to indeterminate nodules with soft labels and transfer learning. From 466 nodule records in 418 patients who underwent molecular testing (Afirma or ThyroSeq), 119 nodules with surgical pathology were used for development and 47 were held out for testing after removing duplicates.
AI.result: AUC 0.73 (95% CI 0.51-0.94) for the DL model versus 0.55 (0.38-0.71) for molecular testing. At the inherited cut-off the DL model was more specific (0.95 vs 0.32; P < 0.001) with higher PPV (0.67 vs 0.21), lower sensitivity (0.44 vs 0.78; P = 0.25) and similar NPV (0.88 vs 0.86). DL output split molecular-positive nodules into a high-risk group (4/6 malignant) and a lower-risk group (3/27 malignant; P = 0.01). Adding the DL term to logistic regression did not improve on DL output alone.
AI.conclusion: Ultrasound DL complemented molecular testing for Bethesda III nodules, in particular by identifying molecular-positive nodules at lower risk of malignancy.

title: Meituan-Robotics-0: A Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Desktop Manipulation
comment: 25 pages. Project page: this https URL ; Code: this https URL
summary: We present Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0), a vision-language-action foundation model and embodied-agent system for stationary-base desktop manipulation. MR0 combines 147 million vision-language samples with 15,060 hours of curated robot trajectories spanning 12 embodiments. A three-stage training recipe aligns multimodal representations with robot behavior through discrete action-token pre-training, transfers these priors to continuous cross-embodiment control through flow-matching mid-training, and adapts the policy through real-world post-training. We introduce Rollback, which pairs replaced policy segments with human corrections to provide positive and negative supervision for CFG-DAgger without value learning or advantage labeling. A unified end-effector interface supports heterogeneous embodiments, while asynchronous action-chunk merging maintains smooth execution under variable inference latency. An event-driven agent maintains persistent task events and reassesses plans when progress or feasibility changes, enabling cross-task retrieval and conditional task resumption. MR0 achieves 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and ranks fifth in the RoboDojo VLA track. Under matched HG-DAgger post-training, MR0 achieves higher average success rate and progress score than $\pi_{0.5}$ across three real-robot tasks. On Ethernet insertion, CFG-DAgger trained with Rollback data reaches 70% success and a progress score of 0.90. Qualitative agent deployments demonstrate cross-task event retrieval and recovery from temporarily unsatisfied task conditions.

AI.tldr: Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0) is a vision-language-action foundation model and embodied agent system for stationary-base desktop manipulation. It achieves 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and ranks fifth in the RoboDojo VLA track.
AI.motivation: The abstract motivates the work by heterogeneous embodiments, variable inference latency, and the need for persistent task planning that reassesses plans when progress or feasibility changes.
AI.method: Three-stage training: discrete action-token pre-training on 147 million vision-language samples and 15,060 hours of robot trajectories across 12 embodiments, flow-matching mid-training for continuous cross-embodiment control, and real-world post-training. Rollback pairs replaced policy segments with human corrections to supply positive and negative supervision for CFG-DAgger without value learning. A unified end-effector interface, asynchronous action-chunk merging and an event-driven agent complete the system.
AI.result: 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and fifth place in the RoboDojo VLA track. Under matched HG-DAgger post-training, higher average success rate and progress score than pi0.5 across three real-robot tasks. On Ethernet insertion, CFG-DAgger trained with Rollback data reaches 70% success and a progress score of 0.90.
AI.conclusion: Large-scale data, staged training and an event-driven agent combine into a foundation model for desktop manipulation, with real-robot gains over pi0.5 under matched post-training.

title: Measurement-Aware Multimodal LLM for No-Reference Low-Dose CT Quality Assessment
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027
summary: No-reference image quality assessment (IQA) of low-dose CT predicts the score that radiologists would assign to a slice without a full-dose reference, as needed to compare dose protocols and denoisers. Trained CT IQA networks agree well with radiologists but output only a score, whereas multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can explain a score but perform poorly on CT when only prompted. We propose a measurement-aware MLLM, built on Qwen3.8-27B, that rates a slice from its image together with six image-domain measurements of noise, sharpness, high-frequency content and streaks, given to the language model as percentiles in text. On the LDCT-IQA 2023 test set, it reaches an Overall score of 2.735, on par with the retrained challenge winner (2.735) and MedSigLIP-FiLM (2.713), and substantially above its base MLLM used as a zero-shot agent. Shuffling the measurements at test time reduces the score by 0.048, mostly through noise, but the same measurements also lead the model to assign higher scores to over-smoothed denoised images.

AI.tldr: A measurement-aware multimodal LLM built on Qwen3.8-27B rates low-dose CT slice quality from the image together with six image-domain measurements given as text percentiles. It reaches an Overall score of 2.735 on the LDCT-IQA 2023 test set, on par with the retrained challenge winner.
AI.motivation: Trained CT IQA networks agree well with radiologists but output only a score, while MLLMs can explain a score but perform poorly on CT when only prompted.
AI.method: The MLLM receives the slice image plus six measurements of noise, sharpness, high-frequency content and streaks, supplied to the language model as percentiles in text.
AI.result: Overall score 2.735, equal to the retrained challenge winner (2.735) and above MedSigLIP-FiLM (2.713), and substantially above its base MLLM used as a zero-shot agent. Shuffling the measurements at test time reduces the score by 0.048, mostly through noise, and the measurements also lead the model to assign higher scores to over-smoothed denoised images.
AI.conclusion: Explicit image-domain measurements make an MLLM competitive for CT quality assessment with explanations, although they can bias scores toward over-smoothed images.

title: On the Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models: A Few Gradient Signs Are All You Need
comment: 98 pages, including supplementary material
summary: The limited supervision available for the few-shot adaptation of vision-language models makes gradient estimation particularly noisy. We find that the gradient magnitudes are severely miscalibrated, while the signs of a small top-magnitude subset remain informative. This motivates SignSparseSGD and DynSignSparseSGD, two state-free optimizers that use gradient magnitudes only to select where to update and fixed-magnitude signs to decide how to update. The static variant fixes the support after the first minibatch. The dynamic variant refreshes it at every step. Across 11 datasets, three CLIP backbones, and five shot levels, the proposed methods are competitive with or outperform parameter-efficient and optimization-based baselines on average, while exhibiting markedly lower sensitivity to long training schedules. They introduce no task-specific modules, maintain no first- or second-moment optimizer states, and use one shared configuration across datasets, backbones, and shot levels. Our code is included in the supplementary materials and will be released upon publication.

AI.tldr: Two state-free optimizers, SignSparseSGD and DynSignSparseSGD, adapt vision-language models in few-shot settings by using gradient magnitudes only to select where to update and fixed-magnitude signs to decide how. Across 11 datasets, three CLIP backbones and five shot levels they are competitive with or outperform parameter-efficient and optimization-based baselines on average.
AI.motivation: Gradient estimation from limited few-shot supervision is noisy, with gradient magnitudes severely miscalibrated, while the signs of a small top-magnitude subset remain informative.
AI.method: The static variant fixes the update support after the first minibatch and the dynamic variant refreshes it at every step. Both introduce no task-specific modules, maintain no first- or second-moment optimizer states, and use one shared configuration across datasets, backbones and shot levels.
AI.result: Competitive with or better than parameter-efficient and optimization-based baselines on average, with markedly lower sensitivity to long training schedules.
AI.conclusion: Sparse sign-based updates offer a simple adaptation method for few-shot vision-language models with a single stable configuration; code is said to be released upon publication.

title: Global Solar Siting from Geospatial Embeddings
comment: Accepted at Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning workshop at NeurIPS 2026. 17 pages, 11 figures
summary: Global solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity is rapidly growing, helping decrease our emissions and dependence on fossil fuels. However, optimally siting a solar plant remains challenging, requiring anticipation of geographical, urban, and infrastructure needs. Current methods rely on multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) using hand-picked geophysical layers and solar-resource products, however these strategies are not geographically transferable and do not capture the practical requirements of solar sites. We use geospatial embeddings, dense vectors representing geophysical properties of a location, to analyse 38,591 existing solar sites and the land they were built on to learn the latent solar suitability signal. We assess a set of linear and non-linear models and select a soft-voting ensemble of a random forest and a multilayer perceptron (RF+MLP ensemble), chosen for accuracy and large scale deployability. Validated against future installations in thirteen countries, the ensemble separates existing solar sites from random land with a median ROC-AUC of 0.90. Compared with published MCDA strategies, the ensemble increases ROC-AUC by 0.06-0.30 in every country. The ranking also concentrates real deployment: the most-suitable 20% of land holds 84% of estimated generation (annual energy yield) and 67% of installed capacity (potential power output). After applying standard siting constraints, 5.6% of global land (9.8% if cropland is permitted) remains highly suited to solar. The global 10 m resolution solar suitability dataset and code can be found here: this https URL.

AI.tldr: The study learns latent solar suitability from geospatial embeddings of 38,591 existing solar sites, using a soft-voting random forest and MLP ensemble that separates existing sites from random land with a median ROC-AUC of 0.90 across thirteen countries. After standard siting constraints, 5.6% of global land remains highly suited to solar.
AI.motivation: Current multi-criteria decision analysis siting relies on hand-picked geophysical layers and solar-resource products that are not geographically transferable and do not capture practical site requirements.
AI.method: Geospatial embeddings, dense vectors representing geophysical properties of a location, are used to analyze existing solar sites and the land they were built on. Linear and non-linear models were assessed, and a soft-voting ensemble of a random forest and a multilayer perceptron was selected for accuracy and large-scale deployability.
AI.result: Validated against future installations in thirteen countries, median ROC-AUC 0.90, and ROC-AUC higher than published MCDA strategies by 0.06-0.30 in every country. The most suitable 20% of land holds 84% of estimated generation and 67% of installed capacity. After standard siting constraints, 5.6% of global land (9.8% if cropland is permitted) remains highly suited.
AI.conclusion: The embedding-based ensemble transfers across geographies and concentrates real deployment better than MCDA, and the paper releases a global 10 m solar suitability dataset and code.

title: UniMore: Fine-Grained Supervision for Unified Understanding and Generation
summary: Unified multimodal models combine image understanding and generation within one system, creating an opportunity to improve both capabilities through paired image--text supervision. We examine the outputs of a pretrained unified model in both directions and observe a loss of specificity: generated images can contain the requested objects with incorrect attributes, while captions identify a scene without expressing its distinguishing details. These failures call for supervision that specifies both the visual content to realize and the descriptive differences to distinguish. We propose UniMore, a post-training method that derives these complementary learning tasks from the fine-grained content of image--text pairs. The generation route predicts grounded crops from their corresponding phrases, matching the scope of the condition and visual target while using the native visual objective. The understanding route combines positive-caption fitting with ranking against captions that omit or alter details, conditioned on the full image. The two routes are optimized independently, and their learned updates are combined into a single unified model without changing its inference procedure. Experiments show gains across multiple understanding and generation benchmarks.
